subject: The Louis De Guzman Blueprint: Why Your Art Needs an Ecosystem to Survive
body:
View this post on the web at https://artmeetsculture.substack.com/p/the-louis-de-guzman-blueprint-why

Louis De Guzman [ https://substack.com/redirect/c9abf77a-2bf3-4946-8784-2b4f9be8d54b?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] doesn’t see art as something confined to a wall.
For more than a decade, the Chicago-based Filipino-American artist has built a visual world rooted in geometric abstraction, memory and movement. His work blends personal history with cultural storytelling, often translating moments from his upbringing into compositions that feel both intimate and expansive. Paintings, collectables, fashion, installation, and design all sit within the same orbit, connected by the same visual language that De Guzman has carefully developed over the years.
Now, that world is expanding once again.
This week marks the launch of IN FULL COLOR [ https://substack.com/redirect/ce5f06cf-f321-4739-995f-4b39d18f5e89?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]™, a new fashion and design venture that extends De Guzman’s practice into a broader lifestyle platform. The debut Spring 2026 collection, titled “Channel Not Available,” represents a new chapter for the artist, one that builds on the foundations of his art practice while pushing further into storytelling through garments and design.
But for De Guzman, this moment is less about reinvention and more about evolution.
When we spoke ahead of the launch, his perspective remained grounded in the same ideas that have shaped his journey from the beginning: family, gratitude, curiosity and community. Success, in his eyes, isn’t defined by milestones alone. It’s about continuing to create experiences that allow the people around you to grow alongside you.
Built From Sacrifice
Before the collaborations, exhibitions and international audiences, there was a story that began decades earlier.
De Guzman’s parents immigrated from the Philippines to the United States in the 1980s, arriving with the same hopes and uncertainties shared by many immigrant families. Their sacrifices became the foundation for everything that followed.
For the artist, that journey continues to shape how he understands success.
“My parents came here in their mid-20s and left their families behind,” he explains. “Seeing that sacrifice has always been a moral compass for me.”
Although his career now spans international exhibitions and major brand collaborations, De Guzman is quick to point out that his family never came from wealth in the traditional sense.
“We didn’t come from a lot,” he says. “But I always say I’m wealthy in experience, in values, in family and in friendship.”
That perspective continues to anchor his practice. Every project, collaboration or exhibition is viewed through the lens of gratitude, a reminder that the opportunities he now experiences are the result of decisions made long before he ever picked up a brush.
The Kid Who Kept Drawing
Like many children growing up in immigrant households, the idea of becoming an artist wasn’t always met with enthusiasm.
De Guzman remembers being seen as the outlier within his extended family, the quiet kid who spent most of his time drawing while others pursued more traditional careers.
“I definitely felt like the black sheep sometimes,” he admits.
But while some relatives questioned his ambitions, his parents did the opposite. His mother introduced him to art early on, often taking him to craft shows where she sold handmade work as a side hustle. Those early experiences left a lasting imprint, one that De Guzman later honoured through a New Balance collaboration dedicated to her.
His father offered a different kind of inspiration. A musician himself, he understood the emotional pull of creative work.
“I remember being around thirteen, and my dad telling me directly, ‘Do what you love.’”
It was a simple statement, but one that shaped everything that followed.
Over time, the scepticism from the extended family began to shift. The same relatives who once questioned his career choice eventually became some of his biggest supporters, asking about upcoming exhibitions and wanting to attend shows.
For De Guzman, those moments carry a quiet sense of validation.
“When you live out your dreams and really believe in yourself, it unlocks so many things,” he says. “But for me, it was never about accolades. It’s about creating experiences that my family and friends can share with me.”
Building a World Beyond the Canvas
Although De Guzman became known through his art practice, fashion has always been part of the picture.
Long before launching IN FULL COLOR™, he studied graphic design and spent years immersed in creative environments tied to Chicago’s streetwear culture. Working around figures such as Don C and observing the influence of artists who successfully crossed into fashion helped shape his understanding of how art could move across disciplines.
“Fashion is art at the end of the day,” he says. “It’s about storytelling.”
That philosophy sits at the centre of IN FULL COLOR™. Rather than simply releasing artist merchandise, the brand is designed as an extension of De Guzman’s broader creative ecosystem , a space where design, narrative and community intersect.
For the artist, the timing finally felt right.
“A lot of these ideas have been sitting in the back pocket for years,” he explains. “Now it feels like the right moment to share them.”
The brand’s debut collection, “Channel Not Available,” captures that idea through nostalgia and imagination. The title references the analogue experience of growing up without constant access to content, when creativity often emerged from boredom or limitation.
“If we didn’t have access to something on TV, we had to find ways to entertain ourselves,” he recalls. “For me, that meant drawing what I wanted to see.”
In today’s hyper-connected world, the concept carries a deeper message. The collection encourages people to reconnect with their own individuality rather than being consumed by digital noise.
“You have to remind yourself that nobody else is like you,” De Guzman says. “You’re one of one.”
Chicago, Full Circle
Although De Guzman’s work now travels internationally, Chicago remains central to his story.
The launch of IN FULL COLOR™ will be followed by a celebratory pop-up at RSVP Gallery, a cultural institution that has played a significant role in shaping the city’s streetwear landscape.
For the artist, returning to the space carries emotional weight.
“I’m very humbled,” he says. “It feels like something that had to happen.”
RSVP Gallery represents more than a retail destination. It’s where De Guzman met collaborators who would later become close friends and creative partners. The space helped foster the community that shaped his early career.
That sense of collective energy continues to guide his approach.
Throughout our conversation, De Guzman repeatedly replaces “I” with “we”, a reflection of how deeply he values the people around him.
“I always say we,” he explains. “Because it’s never just me.”
The team behind his work , including long-time collaborators Austin Neely and Amy Tran , is central to how he builds projects and experiences. Rather than presenting himself as a singular figure, De Guzman sees his practice as something shared.
“It’s always more meaningful to build things with the people you care about,” he says.
When Art Travels Further Than Words
That sense of connection extends far beyond Chicago.
One of the most meaningful milestones in De Guzman’s career came through an exhibition in Seoul, where his work resonated with audiences despite language and cultural differences.
“It reminded me how powerful art can be,” he says.
Some visitors had followed his work for years. Others encountered it for the first time during the exhibition. One fan even drove several hours simply to have a collectable signed.
Moments like that reinforced something De Guzman had long suspected: that art has the ability to communicate across barriers.
“You don’t have to speak the same language to connect,” he explains. “If the work moves someone emotionally, that connection is already there.”
The trip carried an additional layer of meaning as his family joined him for the exhibition, marking their first visit to Korea.
Experiences like that continue to shape how De Guzman measures success.
“It’s about creating moments that once felt impossible,” he says.
Still Thinking Like the Kid in the Kitchen
Despite the scale his career has reached, De Guzman still finds himself thinking about the younger version of himself who once spent hours drawing at the kitchen table.
If that version could see everything he has built today, the artist believes the reaction would be simple.
“He’d probably be excited,” he says with a smile. “But he’d also be like, ‘Wait… really?’”
For De Guzman, that younger self remains an important reminder of why the work started in the first place.
“I’d just want to tell him to keep drawing,” he says. “You’re going to do something with it.”
Extending the Dream Board
Looking ahead, De Guzman isn’t focused on a single destination.
Instead, he describes his future plans as an ever-expanding dream board, one that continues to grow as new ideas and opportunities emerge.
Still, there are a few ambitions he hopes to bring to life in the coming years.
“I’d love to do a show in Europe,” he says. “London would be amazing.”
Beyond traditional exhibitions, he also envisions immersive environments that blend art, design and experience , projects that invite audiences to step inside the world he has spent years building.
“I’d love to take over a space like a hotel or public environment,” he explains. “Where everything comes together, the art, the atmosphere, the experience.”
For an artist whose work is rooted in storytelling, that vision feels like a natural next step.
Showing Up Every Day
If there’s one piece of advice De Guzman returns to repeatedly, it’s the importance of persistence.
The modern art world may be evolving, with artists increasingly building their own platforms outside traditional gallery systems, but the core principle remains the same.
“You just have to keep bettering yourself,” he says.
Moments of uncertainty are inevitable, but De Guzman believes they often signal the beginning of something new.
“When the well runs dry, it doesn’t mean you’re finished,” he explains. “It means something else is about to start.”
He encourages emerging artists to hold onto their ideas, even the ones they initially dismiss.
“Don’t throw anything away,” he says. “Those ideas might come back when you need them most.”
At its core, his philosophy remains simple: every sketch, every experiment and every day carries value.
“Everything serves a purpose,” he says. “You just have to show up and get one per cent better.”
IN FULL COLOR [ https://substack.com/redirect/ce5f06cf-f321-4739-995f-4b39d18f5e89?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]™ launches Friday, March 13, with the debut Spring 2026 collection “Channel Not Available,” followed by an in-store pop-up at RSVP Gallery in Chicago.

subject: See you at noon...
body:
Today at noon Central.

If you're building anything significant — a business, a ministry, a legacy — and it's structured as an LLC, 501(c)(3), or any statutory entity...

You're building inside Babylon's jurisdiction.
Which means when the system collapses, everything you built goes with it.

Bradley Logan and I are going live in a few hours to show you the alternative:

The Trinity Model.
508(c)(1)(a) + PMA + Ecclesiastical Trust = Complete exit from man's system, 100% legal, zero connection to Caesar's jurisdiction.

This is the same structure we used to build an entire village in Costa Rica. No taxes. No state authority. Complete sovereignty under Divine Law.

Today's masterclass covers:
✅ Why your LLC can't protect what's coming
✅ How the 508 gives you spiritual jurisdiction (the Queen on the chessboard)
✅ Lawful chess moves to transition existing structures
✅ How to steward Kingdom resources without permission from Babylon

Bradley spent 33 years as an attorney. He knows both systems. 

He knows where the traps are.
Join the live masterclass here → click to enter the event room

Starts at noon Central. Don't miss it.

- Jonathan

P.S. — "Come out of her, my people." This is how.

subject: How to Train Your Sheeple
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/how-to-train-your-sheeple

Throughout history powerful institutions have understood a simple truth about human behavior. Large populations are easier to guide when they are distracted, divided, and emotionally manipulated. The term sheeple is often used to describe citizens who follow narratives without question, accept authority without scrutiny, and react emotionally rather than critically.
This article does not celebrate that process. Instead it exposes the tactics that have been used repeatedly by governments, propagandists, marketers, and power brokers to shape public behavior.
Understanding these methods is the first step toward avoiding them.
Step One: Control the Narrative
People tend to believe what they hear repeatedly. If a message is delivered often enough and from sources perceived as credible it becomes accepted as truth even when the evidence is thin.
Narratives are reinforced through repetition, emotional storytelling, and selective presentation of facts. Complicated issues are simplified into slogans so the audience does not feel the need to investigate further.
When a population hears only one dominant explanation for events questioning begins to feel unusual.
Step Two: Saturate the Information Space
Information overload is one of the most effective control mechanisms. When citizens are bombarded with constant news, alerts, opinions, and crises they lose the time and mental energy required to verify facts.
The result is passive consumption rather than active thinking.
Confusion leads to dependence. When people feel overwhelmed they look for someone else to interpret reality for them.
Step Three: Create Emotional Triggers
Fear, anger, and outrage move crowds faster than logic.
If people are frightened they will often accept policies or restrictions they would normally reject. If they are angry they can be directed toward convenient enemies.
Emotional responses bypass rational thinking. That is why propaganda often relies on shocking images, dramatic language, and urgent messaging.
Step Four: Divide the Population
A united population asks difficult questions. A divided population argues with itself.
By encouraging tribal identities and constant conflict between groups attention shifts away from those actually holding power. Citizens become busy fighting one another rather than examining systems and decisions.
Division weakens collective awareness.
Step Five: Reward Conformity
Human beings are social creatures and naturally seek acceptance within their community.
Modern technology amplifies this instinct. Approval comes in the form of likes, shares, and social reinforcement. Dissent on the other hand often brings ridicule or isolation.
When people see that questioning authority carries social consequences many will simply remain silent.
Step Six: Repeat the Cycle
The most effective conditioning happens slowly over time. Narratives are reinforced, critics are marginalized, and emotional responses are continually triggered.
Eventually many individuals stop questioning the framework altogether and begin to operate within it automatically.
This is the point where independent thinking becomes rare.
Breaking the Cycle
The purpose of understanding these tactics is not cynicism but awareness.
A society that values freedom requires citizens who ask questions, verify information, and resist manipulation driven by fear or group pressure.
Critical thinking is the antidote to manufactured obedience. The moment people pause, investigate, and refuse to be emotionally herded is the moment the so called training of sheeple begins to fail.

subject: Reminder: Action required to keep your Concepts account
body:
Action Required to keep your Concepts account       Please sign in
to keep your Concepts account

  
 Infinite, flexible sketching.
    Hi

 We noticed you haven't signed in to your Concepts account with the email
address *joshualeewillems@gmail.com* for more than a year. As a reminder,
Concepts is an infinite canvas sketching app and you created a free account
some time ago. We like to keep things tidy on our side and remove accounts
that are no longer being used.

 This does not affect your drawings or purchases, but does impact account
sync between your devices. You have two options:

   - If you would like to keep your account, please sign in to Concepts via
the app. To do this, open Concepts, go to the Gallery and tap the account
icon in the status bar. You can be using Concepts without being signed in
as an account is not needed to use Concepts. So, please check that you are
signed in.
  - If you do not sign in, then two weeks from today we will delete your
Concepts account and all of its associated data. Note that your drawings
and purchases are not stored on your account and therefore will not be
deleted, they remain on your device with the installed app.
 
 Please reply to this email if you have questions, we're happy to help.

 Thanks,

 The Concepts Team

subject: 'Touching Solid Ground'
body:
View this post on the web at https://jeremydjohnson.substack.com/p/touching-solid-ground

A recent post by contemplative mystic Cynthia Bourgeault  pivoted her discussion on the planetary crisis from an exploration of consciousness and worldview (“A Gebserian Take [ https://substack.com/redirect/5a4fd3c9-7588-4e42-882a-ae3445eb320d?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]”) to the deep-time perspective Jesuit scholar and mystic Pierre Teilhard de Chardin. During our conversation last month, we talked about the spiritual import of Jean Gebser, who understood our present as a time of breakdown and breakthrough of worldviews (or ‘structures’ of consciousness, as Gebser would assert). 
What we need is a new consciousness of time, and so it’s a good thing, then, that a new consciousness of time seems to have already taken hold of us in nearly every facet of modern life. 
Here’s the catch: the new time is experienced indirectly as a kind of cultural unconscious. It shows up as ecological catastrophe (solastalgia, ‘mourning the future’) or the rampant ‘time crisis’ of neoliberalism (which emphasizes the opposite pull towards the past, or ‘formal nostalgia’). 
In our call, Bourgeault memorably suggested that “attention is the new time,” and that it is precisely through contemplative practices of reclaiming time, attending to the present, that the presence of the new has its chance to ripen in us.
Teilhard, no less temporal, adds another contribution of depth to this exploration. Gebser’s whole project emphasizes transformations of human consciousness, but Teilhard, who is inspired by the work of Henri Bergson, is keen to describe a sweeping history of planetary evolution. So while we should ‘stay with the trouble,’ as Donna Haraway reminds us, Teilhard isn’t asking us to bypass the trouble but touch something like “solid ground.” As Bourgeault writes,
For at this scale it becomes clear that our only real hope of a breakthrough will come when a critical mass of human beings begin to exercise their capacity to think planetarily—i.e., as a single species: rising above nationalist divisions, theological story-telling, sacred-cow histories, and ideological illusions to begin to work as whole greater than the sum of its parts breaking into totally new ground.
I think this long view of planetary evolution is precisely what becomes available when we attend to our present. Perhaps this is much as Bergsonian notion as Gebserian: that as we tend to the present, the present exfoliates time in all directions. We deepen our capacity to perceive time as undivided, but nonetheless intuitive, intelligible, and relational. Perhaps it is this capacity to be with time in both its most immediate and most vast, most distant sense that helps us begin to perceive relations between events in an asynchronous and networked fashion. Perhaps this is the kind of thing that novelists like Frank Herbert speculatively intuited in his Dune books as prescience (although imperfectly, as it can’t just be the achievement of one individual). In any case, if homo sapiens are to continue to have a place in this world, developing a temporal and planetary style of thought becomes a matter of urgent necessity.
This kind of thinking is not thought in the sense of the cogito of Western philosophy. Its position is no longer the mastermind, the arbiter of the real and divider of space. Because of the fundamental precarity of Earth’s living systems (and in a more metaphysical and Bergsonian sense, the sheer creativity and radical newness that comprises the flow of time) we can never exhaustively know what will unfold, or what latent consequences our actions will befall. So we must remain open, receptive, and listen to the reverberations of the whole complex web of interrelationships. This is how we learn to walk with the world. This is how we take our first tentative steps into the future.
Gebser’s insights on time help us to regard Teilhard’s sweeping evolutionary vision with a greater sense of groundedness and relationality. And Gebser helps us to mind the very nature of this exercise: whenever we think of ourselves and our present world in the context of millions, or even billions of years, we are engaging in practices of imaginative, temporal fabulation. Deep time helps us perceive the present in a new light, but as Gebser reminds us and as Bergson consistently reiterates, time is not space, and the new mutation aspires to regard the undivided present as the integral relation between past and future. Putting it succinctly: the future is present too. 
But to bring it back home: what sort of future? 
As Bourgeault talks about, we are thinking about all this in order to better contemplate the true precarity of it all. The chance that it won’t work out for us (as in all of us, our common Earth), and the creative becoming of matter will continue on elsewhere in the universe (in the words of Star Trek’s captain Kirk: “out there… thataway [ https://substack.com/redirect/5c341ad1-62c8-44a5-bf46-6e31deab62b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]"). And so I would like to close this morning writing exercise with one more thought. 
We merely glanced at it earlier when I talked about how the future often arrives in unconscious form as crisis. It shows up where we wouldn’t think to look. It can be found in the peculiar novelties that disrupt business as usual, and tend to occur when living through a time of civilizational collapse. Like Bourgeault suggests, let us stay with the dark for a moment. For it is in the broken places, the places of noise and rupture and even heartbreak, that the new finds its way into our world. 
Since we live in an age of slow-motion catastrophe, our culture has become flooded with neologisms, all of which are attempting to name this new structure of feeling (I will forgo a digression on terms like ‘polycrisis’ or ‘metacrisis’ for now). 
As mentioned earlier, solastalgia describes what it feels like to mourn for vanishing species and ecological landscapes affected by the climate crisis (Sophie Strand  has a profoundly moving meditation on solastalgia and the last male Kauaʻi ʻōʻō bird here [ https://substack.com/redirect/ae366b8b-f953-4026-b0b8-4e59a8be20e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]). It describes something that is still present, but its presence also contains an absence, or what we could call a becoming-absent (echoing J.R.R. Tolkien’s Middle-Earth notion of ‘the long defeat’). Think of it like the Buddhist notion of dukkha, stated in future imperfect tense. 
I bring this word up again because it’s directly relevant to our question of how stay in contact with Bourgeault’s “solid ground,” and how we can find a way to hold the precarity and possibility of our times with both a sense of grace and a new forms of agency.
Perhaps that sounds like too much of an ask for such times, and we should instead trust our heart’s grief, allow ourselves to unravel. I think this is good medicine, too. But I want to suggest that trusting our grief, and living the new, are not separate things. In the very depths of our grief for a vanishing world, other futures are already present. The future arrives in the shape of our grief.
This is why it’s important to keep sifting through our culture’s present-day attempts to name our experience of the ecological crisis and process the feeling of living through a fundamental collapse of worldview. Whether we are looking artistic expressions like new music genres, narrative expressions like science fiction, or theoretical expressions like philosophy (i.e., posthumanism), what we find is that at the periphery and amidst the noise of the capitalist present, the music of planetary culture has already begun singing.
Historian William Irwin Thompson was fond of saying that “we tell more than we know.” This applies not only to our ancient myths, but our modern day art and culture making. Contemporary culture is dominated by creations of ‘formal nostalgia,’ a retrospective gaze—but even our attempts to escape the present and return to a romanticized past, to a time where the future was still open and people still had faith in the future-as-progress—are already employing a fundamentally weirder temporality (they are haunted by the lost futures of modernity, futures which they wish to resurrect). Even those who would be against such an ecological worldview, and would prefer to have nothing to do with any of this kind of thinking, are imbricated in it. They are already mutants. Nostalgia tells more than it knows. 
We need to consider how both nostalgia and solastalgia are (partial) manifestations of Gebser’s ‘integral’ mutation, and Teilhard’s planetization. Jumping back and forth between past and future, they begin to employ a more elastic and relational time, a weird planetary time that exists beyond the clock.
When we attend to the present, we begin to sense how the future as well as the past are real and effectual. Ecological futures, especially, have become more real for us these days. One could readily argue, as philosophers like Srecko Horvat do in After the Apocalypse, that climate futures have been radically transforming our subjectivity. The grief many of us feel for species like the Kauaʻi ʻōʻō bird is becoming kind of ‘productive melancholy,’ as Walter Benjamin wrote about, empowering us to act before it is too late, and subvert the deadly momentum of the neoliberal present.
As a closing thought, I want to suggest that our climate crisis is, irreducibly, a temporal crisis, first set ablaze during the Industrial Revolution. The very attempt to come to grips with what is happening to us and through us requires the awakening of a wholly new consciousness of time.
Good thing, then, that this new temporality already seems to be stirring in us.
Postscript
“I don’t know. On Mondays… I think that we are experiencing a discontinuous transition from one world-system to another, a ‘catastrophe.’ On Tuesdays… I feel better and think that it is going to be a transition with continuity, one like the previous transition from medievalism to modernism. On Sundays, I try to rest and seek a contemplative detachment… If I am forced to choose one scenario over the other, I would rather work politically for a cultural transformation with continuity from one world-system to another, than join a survivalist community or wait to be picked up by a flying saucer.”
— William Irwin Thompson, Pacific Shift
So how do you or I live in such impossible, paradoxical times, where time itself seems to have become a thick and imbricated present? In the next installment, I will unpack this inquiry further, but for now I want to suggest that regardless of how the ecological crisis unfolds, regardless of whether or not it will be a catastrophe or a smoother transition from one world system to another, we ought to live as if planetary futures were already present. Real and intimate and substantive. 
If the experience of solastalgia can be so transformative, then we ought to keep turning it over while retaining its temporal structure: other, more constructive, futures, planetary futures which, even if they are after an apocalypse, are not vanishing but coalescing, and they too are present. These other futures shape us, and as Mallarme says, ripen from the morrow. 
In my manuscript and for convenience, I am calling this the practice of integral futuring. Feel a little bit of discomfort with this science fiction bent? That’s good. We need more mutants right now. More than ever.
If the shape of crisis is fundamentally temporal, entangling past and future, in what ways can we begin living this new cultural mentality in forms that are agentic, constructive, and empowering in the ruins of the neoliberal present?

subject: Trump just let Ticketmaster off the hook
body:
Ticketmaster’s exclusive agreements with venues have been a thorn in the side of musicians and sports fans for decades.

Joshua willems,

Instead of taking Live Nation-Ticketmaster to trial, Trump’s Department of Justice just let them off the hook.

After years of building a case that Live Nation-Ticketmaster should be broken up, and one week into the trial brought initially by President Biden’s DOJ and dozens of states, the federal government announced that it has reached a settlement with Live Nation.

More than two dozen states are rejecting this settlement, claiming that it does not do enough to rein in Live Nation’s greed. In fact, the $280 million settlement represents just four days of revenue for a corporation that raked in more than $25 billion last year alone.

Ticketmaster and Live Nation have destroyed the concert experience. They get away with it because they control more than 60 of the top 100 amphitheaters in the U.S. and roughly 80 percent of primary ticketing.

Send a message to your State Attorney General now and urge them to either join or remain on the lawsuit to break up Live Nation-Ticketmaster and hold this greedy monopoly accountable.

SIGN & SEND

Through multiple investigative reports, More Perfect Union has been holding Live Nation-Ticketmaster accountable for years. Our investigative reporting found that ticket prices for the biggest acts between 1970 and 1989 cost around $45. Today you’re paying exorbitant service fees and indie venues are getting squeezed, all because two corporations gobbled up the industry.

Ticketmaster’s exclusive agreements with venues have been a thorn in the side of musicians and sports fans for decades. Pearl Jam testified about it before Congress all the way back in 1995. Instead of taking action then, the government allowed Ticketmaster to merge with concert promotion behemoth Live Nation in 2010. Now, Live Nation-Ticketmaster sits between artists and fans and rips off both sides. This problem has finally become too big to ignore.

Fans shouldn’t have to sign away their rights any time they want to go see their favorite band or team, especially not when they’re already paying through the nose!

Click here to watch our exclusive deep dive into the history of concerts over the last 70 years and how corporate greed turned one of the most populist forms of entertainment into a luxury good, then sign and send a direct message to your State Attorney General now.

Together, we’re urging states to continue their antitrust lawsuit against Live Nation-Ticketmaster for industry monopolization and other unlawful conduct that thwarts competition in markets across the live entertainment industry.

In solidarity,

-Faiz

subject: When Governments Act Like Terrorists They Create Terrorists
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/when-governments-act-like-terrorists

Terrorism does not appear in a vacuum. It grows out of pain, loss, humiliation, and cycles of violence that can stretch across generations. When governments wage war in ways that devastate civilian populations, destroy homes, and shatter families, the consequences do not end when the bombs stop falling. Those consequences often take the form of anger, resentment, and radicalization.
One of the harsh lessons of modern conflict is that overwhelming military force can sometimes create the very enemies it claims to defeat.
The war in Iraq became one of the most controversial examples of this reality. What began as a military campaign justified by claims of weapons of mass destruction turned into a long occupation that destabilized an entire region. Cities were destroyed. Infrastructure collapsed. Civilian casualties mounted. Millions were displaced from their homes. Entire families were wiped out in bombings, raids, and crossfire.
For those who survived, the war was not a geopolitical debate. It was deeply personal.
Imagine a child who loses parents in a bombing. Imagine a brother who watches his home collapse with relatives inside. Imagine growing up in an environment where drones hum overhead and foreign soldiers patrol your streets. In that environment, grief and anger become powerful forces. Extremist recruiters understand this. They exploit that pain, telling survivors that violence is the only language their enemies understand.
This is how cycles of terror are born.
When powerful nations conduct wars without clear accountability for civilian harm, they risk becoming what many victims perceive as terrorists themselves. To a grieving family, the difference between a bomb dropped by a military jet and a bomb planted by a militant may feel meaningless. Both took loved ones. Both destroyed lives.
This does not justify terrorism. Nothing can justify the deliberate targeting of innocent civilians. But understanding how terrorism grows is essential if the world hopes to stop it.
Many intelligence and military experts have acknowledged that heavy handed warfare can fuel insurgencies. Every civilian death can create multiple new enemies. Every destroyed village can become a recruiting poster for extremist groups.
Some critics argue that certain powerful interests benefit from perpetual conflict. Endless war creates massive profits for defense contractors. It expands surveillance powers at home. It allows governments to justify security policies that might otherwise face public resistance. Whether one believes in coordinated intent or simply systemic incentives, the result often looks the same. Wars continue long after their original justification collapses.
The tragedy is that ordinary people on all sides pay the price.
American soldiers return home with physical and psychological wounds. Iraqi civilians live with the devastation of their communities. Families across the world bury their dead while politicians debate strategy.
Breaking the cycle requires honesty. It requires acknowledging that military dominance alone cannot bring stability or peace. It requires understanding that bombing a society into submission often plants the seeds of the next conflict.
If governments truly want to defeat terrorism, they must recognize a difficult truth. Violence that destroys innocent lives does not eliminate extremism. It feeds it.
Peace is not built through fear. It is built through justice, accountability, and respect for human life.
Until that lesson is learned, the world risks repeating the same tragic pattern again and again.

subject:
The Gathering Storm Rumors Investigations and the Question of the 2020
 Election
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-gathering-storm-rumors-investigations

For years the debate surrounding the 2020 United States presidential election has remained one of the most contentious issues in modern American politics. Allegations counter allegations audits and investigations have circulated across media platforms political institutions and public discourse. While many official bodies have maintained that the election outcome was legitimate new developments suggest the story may not yet be finished.
Recent reports indicate that federal investigators are expanding a criminal probe into suspected election irregularities. According to sources familiar with the investigation the Federal Bureau of Investigation has quietly obtained large volumes of voting records from Maricopa County Arizona the most populous county in the state and one that has long been at the center of election related controversy.
The records were reportedly obtained through a federal grand jury subpoena. Sources say the bureau is receiving terabytes of electronic election data from the county. The subpoena comes only weeks after federal agents executed a raid on a warehouse near Atlanta Georgia seizing ballots connected to the 2020 election in Fulton County.
Together these developments suggest that investigators may be taking a deeper look at election processes in several key jurisdictions.
Arizona Back in the Spotlight
Concerns surrounding election administration in Arizona are not new. In the aftermath of the 2020 election the Arizona State Senate conducted a lengthy audit of voting procedures and ballot records in Maricopa County.
That audit concluded that while the final vote totals themselves were not definitively overturned investigators found numerous irregularities that raised serious questions about procedures and oversight.
Among the most controversial findings was an estimate suggesting that more than 200000 ballots with potentially mismatched signatures may have been counted without undergoing proper review. The county had previously acknowledged approximately 25000 signature mismatches that required curing which is a process used to verify voter intent.
Supporters of the audit argued that the discrepancy revealed a significant vulnerability in the system. Critics countered that the findings were overstated and that the audit did not ultimately change the election results.
The dispute has remained unresolved fueling ongoing political tension in the state.
A New Layer of Federal Scrutiny
The current FBI investigation appears to be examining whether certain irregularities crossed the line from administrative error into possible violations of federal law.
In an affidavit related to the Georgia ballot seizure an FBI agent stated that investigators had substantiated some irregularities in how votes were handled in Fulton County following the 2020 election. The bureau is now attempting to determine whether any of those irregularities were intentional acts that violated election laws.
Some allegations have been disproven during the investigation according to the affidavit. Others however were reportedly confirmed through documentation and admissions by local officials.
The probe now appears to be expanding.
Sources familiar with the investigation say federal authorities are examining data not only from the 2020 election but also from more recent elections including the 2024 cycle.
Election observers from both major political parties reportedly submitted reports documenting unusual conditions at a ballot storage facility in Arizona during the 2024 election period. According to those reports both blank and completed absentee ballots were observed stored in the same location.
Photographs and documentation were reportedly included in the observer report.
While the report itself has not been publicly released lawmakers reviewing the material have suggested it contains significant information that could warrant further investigation.
Rumors of a Long Running Court Case
Beyond the FBI probe another theory circulating among legal observers and political commentators has captured growing attention.
Some believe that the United States Supreme Court may have quietly kept a case related to the 2020 election open for years without public resolution. According to this speculation the Court could be waiting for additional evidence or criminal findings before addressing constitutional questions related to the election process.
There is no official confirmation that such a case exists in the manner described. However the rumor persists in legal and political circles particularly as new investigations continue to unfold.
If such a case were ever formally addressed it could raise profound questions about the legal doctrine that fraud vitiates everything. This longstanding principle in law holds that if fraud is proven to have occurred in a process the legitimacy of that process can be nullified.
In the context of elections the implications would be enormous.
The Stakes for the Nation
Election integrity is the foundation of democratic legitimacy. For that reason both allegations of fraud and allegations of unfounded conspiracy carry serious consequences.
If investigators ultimately conclude that irregularities were administrative mistakes or misinterpretations of procedures the findings may reinforce existing conclusions about the election.
However if criminal conduct were proven to have occurred in a coordinated or intentional manner the consequences could reverberate across American political and legal institutions for decades.
Either outcome would carry significant implications for public trust.
A Moment of Uncertainty
The expansion of federal subpoenas the seizure of ballots and the review of massive volumes of election data suggest that investigators are still examining unanswered questions.
Whether these inquiries will uncover wrongdoing clarify misunderstandings or simply reaffirm previous conclusions remains unknown.
What is certain is that the issue has not entirely faded from the national stage.
For many Americans the coming months may determine whether the controversies surrounding the 2020 election finally reach a definitive resolution or whether they deepen further.
If the principle that fraud nullifies everything were ever invoked in relation to a national election the consequences would reshape American history.
Until investigators complete their work and courts weigh the evidence the nation remains in a state of watchful uncertainty.

subject: [PODCAST #631] 👉 How Family Rules Shaped Your Personality Type
body:
Discover how your family’s hidden rules may still be influencing the way you think, feel, and navigate life today.
 

Live Podcast Recording — Nashville, TN
Saturday, March 21 @ 7:30pm → Get Tickets

 

Hi Joshua,

 

Some of the most powerful forces shaping your personality were never spoken out loud.

 

In this week’s episode, we explore how family systems create unspoken “rules of engagement” around sensing, feeling, thinking, and intuition, and how those rules may have shaped the way your personality developed.

 

This conversation offers a powerful lens for understanding not just your personality, but the environment that shaped how you learned to express it in life.
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕
 

In this week's episode, we explore:

  • How family dynamics influence you & which parts of your personality feel safe, valued, or off-limits

  • Why type profiles only tell part of the story, and why context matters

  • How your family may have taught you to regulate stress through one preferred channel

  • Why some parts of your type became strengths while others were hidden, delayed, or misunderstood

  • How understanding your family’s default patterns can help you make sense of your growth today

Discover how your family’s hidden rules may still be influencing the way you think, feel, and navigate life today.

 

👉 We’d love to hear from you: What rules of engagement shaped your family system, and how do you see them showing up in your life now?

<— Hit reply and share your experience with us.

 

We released this podcast in both video and audio this week.
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕
 


Much Love,

Joel Mark Witt & Antonia Dodge
Co-Founders | Personality Hacker
 

PS -  Join Us for a Live Personality Hacker Podcast in Nashville

On Saturday, March 21, we are taking the show on the road and inviting you to join us for a live audience experience and podcast recording near Nashville, Tennessee.

The last time we were in Nashville we hosted a live podcast you can watch here.

 

We will gather a small group of like-minded people to record the podcast together, then open things up for Q&A and discussion around personality type and personal growth.

 

Afterward, we'd love for you to stay for an informal mixer where we can hang out, talk with other attendees, spend time with us and our team, and keep the conversation going.

 

We have hosted live events, podcasts, and meetups in places like Atlanta, Chicago, New York City, Hollywood, Seattle, Austin, Denver, Toronto, Valencia, and Copenhagen. Every time, we meet thoughtful people from this community and get to continue the conversation in person.

 

It's such an awesome experience... Antonia and I would LOVE to meet you in person.

 

This is an in-person only event and space is limited.

subject: [Care Ministry: Prayer Sheet] TLC Prayer Sheet 3/10
body:
TLC Prayer Sheet 3/10

Recently there was a situation where I was really struggling
with envy. Enough that it haunted my early morning thoughts and
the devil whispered his lies of, "how unfair, how cruel, that
they would get what you wanted. You deserved it more. They did
nothing for it. And look at the cost you're still paying for the
lot you did get." I must confess they were very tempting lies.
Because they contained just enough essence of little truths, and
spoke directly to my pride and my wounds.

I tried to convince myself, "but remember those lessons you
learned, and that humble spirit you had that drew you to
Christ?"

And I kinda held onto those thoughts, but the whispers of, "it's
just so unfair," echoed in my heart.

Lately I have been reading Keep a Quiet Heart, a collection of
devotional readings by Elisabeth Elliot. And she is the person
that could say, "it's just so unfair, and most people wouldn't
even blame her." She was tragically widowed twice over after only
being married to each man a few years. Her first husband was
killed while doing mission work. Her second died of cancer. Yet,
she doesn't say that, instead she writes:

"...God has allowed in the lives of each of us some sort of loss,
the withdrawal of something we valued, in order that we might
learn to offer ourselves a little more willingly, to allow the
touch of death on one more thing we have clutched so tightly, and
thus know fullness and freedom and joy that much sooner. We're
not naturally inclined to love God and seek His Kingdom. Trouble
may help us-that is, it may tip us over, put some pressure on us,
lean us in the right direction."

So while things are sometimes unfair, or unjust or just plain
broken and sad, we can have assurance that it all points us in
the right direction-towards what really lasts and really
matters-fullness and freedom in Christ.

Gas Prices Fluctuate After Iran Conflict Intensifies: The average
price of gasoline in the United States increased to $3.48 per
gallon on Monday, according to AAA. The shift came after the US
and Israel carried out more strikes against Iran over the
weekend. That marked an almost 17% jump since the conflict began
on February 28, the highest prices since 2024. The price of oil
also pushed to over $100 a barrel for the first time in four
years, marking a more than 40% increase since the conflict began.
The spike comes amidst a growing concern that the conflict will
constrain energy supplies, in part because Iran has shut down the
Strait of Hormuz, the world’s most critical oil supply passage.
In 2024, the Strait averaged 20 million barrels of oil per day in
transit, supplying approximately 20% of the world’s population.
But late Monday, oil reversed after President Donald Trump told a
reporter the war was nearly complete, with prices dropping below
$90 by mid-day. US officials had discussed with fellow Group of
Seven members multiple options to help curb rising oil prices,
according to Reuters. They reportedly include a joint release of
each country’s strategic petroleum reserves, restricting US
exports, intervening in oil futures markets and more.      On

this month,” which resolves at the end of March. Ready to hedge

subject: "Marriage Tools for Connection" Parent Seminar Sun 3/15 + Passover Seder Sun 3/29
body:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/tlc/twin-lakes-kids-thisweek-6429879?e=7d63af6d69)
https://tlc.org

Amazing Awana Grand Prix!

Last weekend, we held our Annual Awana Grand Prix!!! So many wonderful kids and families were on hand to enjoy the races and have a blast together! Thanks so everyone who helped make it happen!!

March & April 2026
* TLK Teaching: “The Great Love Race” (https://mcusercontent.com/1abe188c7cc5e4aa6b0f74d9a/files/c999d170-979c-f470-58c6-e7d684265d48/family_resource_mar_2026_1_.pdf)
* Sun Mar 15: “Better Together”: Parenting Seminars (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2051/responses/new) (two options)
+ Marriage Tools for Connection in Chaos
+ Single Parenting in Community
* Sun Mar 29:
+ “Finding Balance in Connection” (http://tlc.org/parentadventure) Parenting Seminar @ 11am
+ TLC Passover Seder (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2042/responses/new) (family-friendly!) @ 5pm
* Sun April 5: EASTER 2026!
* SAVE THE DATES: Wed 4/16 - 4 week Positive Discipline Class with Colleen Murphy starts!
* SUMMER
+ June + July: Kruz Kidz @ TLC - register now! (https://kruzkidz.com/)
+ June 15-18: TLC Pre-school Vacation Bible School (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2025/responses/new) @ TLC
+ July 15 -18: Mother/Daughters Ranch Camp (https://www.mounthermon.org/events/kc-moms-daughters-ranch) @ Kidder Creek


https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2051/responses/new

OPTION 1 - Better Together

"Marriage Tools for Connection in the Chaos"

Join Suzi & Jim Josselyn—parents of three grown kids—as they share insights from 33 years of marriage. Discover practical, Christ-centered tools that have helped them stay intentionally connected through the busyness of life, the challenges of raising kids, and the call to follow Jesus faithfully.

About Jim & Suzi: Jim serves as a TLC pastor, with decades of experience serving in family, marriage, and recovery ministry. Suzi is a Christian educator + non-profit CEO. They have 3 young adult children.

OPTION 2 - Better Together

"Single Parenting in Community"

Connect with Yolanda Beaudoin, a single mom with 4 grown children + TLK's Children's Ministry Director, who will lead a discussion to help connect and encourage single parents!

About Yolanda: Yolanda serves as TLC’s Kid’s Ministry Director and on the board of a local non-profit; she raised her 4 adult children as a single parent.

Timing:
* 10:15-10:45am = Hang out time @ big TLC playground (free coffee!)
* 10:45am = Kid’s Ministry drop off
* 11am - 12:30pm = Parenting Seminar

Location:  Monschke Hall, Main Room
RSVP for “BETTER TOGETHER” (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2051/responses/new)

https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2042/responses/new

A Seder is the traditional Passover celebration meal; Jesus hosted a Seder with his disciples before his crucifixion and resurrection.

TLC is excited to host a Passover Seder meal (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2042/responses/new) , an interactive experience featuring speaker Josh Sofaer with Jews for Jesus. Josh will explain the significance for Christians of the Passover dinner, which has been celebrated for over 4,000 years.

Sunday Mar 29, 5-7pm is an all-ages are welcome (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2042/responses/new) , and we encourage you to bring your children to this family-friendly event.  Age appropriate activities for younger children will be provided.

Want to serve with your kids to help make the Seder happen?! Contact maryjo@tlc.org (mailto:maryjo@tlc.org) for more info!
Register for Sun 3/29 Seder Experience (https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/2042/responses/new)

Easter is Coming!
For everyone who likes to plan ahead, here are our Easter Weekend service times:
* Good Friday: April 3rd, 6:30pm
* Easter Services:
+ Saturday, April 4th, 4:30pm & 6:00pm
+ Sunday, April 5th, 8:30am, 10am and 11:30am.


https://mcusercontent.com/1abe188c7cc5e4aa6b0f74d9a/files/671d5f71-16c9-b136-dba1-ba1d46a2ad3c/family_resource_jan_2026.pdf

TLK Teaching Theme: Jesus LOVES

Throughout our stories this month, the love of Jesus shines bright. Jesus’ unconditional love reaches beyond all boundaries. Jesus knew the suffering ahead, yet His love compelled Him to move forward for our sake. Even in the pain of betrayal, Jesus remained faithful—His love never wavered. Through every act, Jesus showed us a love that is constant, sacrificial, and beyond measure.

Elementary Memory Verse:

As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Abide in My love. (John 15:9)

Early Childhood Memory Verse:

Abide in my Love. (John 15:9)
Family Resource PDF for “JESUS LOVES” (https://mcusercontent.com/1abe188c7cc5e4aa6b0f74d9a/files/c999d170-979c-f470-58c6-e7d684265d48/family_resource_mar_2026_1_.pdf)

https://twinlakeschurch.ccbchurch.com/goto/forms/1785/responses/new

PARENT OF NEURODIVERGENT (PON) SUPPORT

Can you still
learn piano if
the teacher can’t see your hands?

With the addition of Airwave, ROLI Learn is the only piano-learning app that can see, as well as hear, what and how you play. But does it really matter? And what does it mean for the effectiveness of other apps? To find out, we pitted our AI Music Coach against Liz, a real piano teacher — and a good one at that.
 
But we didn’t exactly play fair; while the AI Music Coach was able to scan our learners’ hands in incredible detail with Airwave, Liz had to rely on nothing more than her wits and a good-old-fashioned telephone.

subject: Unshazamable
body:
View this post on the web at https://robwalker.substack.com/p/unshazamable

* Great responses are coming in for March’s Savor of the Month [ https://substack.com/redirect/6eaad94b-b0e6-4370-aaed-a5078b42e434?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] prompt: Public Text [ https://substack.com/redirect/c11adb47-da4f-4fc0-8b87-a54a6013f323?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]. Join in here [ https://substack.com/redirect/3897e824-85e3-49d2-8601-266d346bca38?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]!
Today, a couple of open-earedness [ https://substack.com/redirect/66165b84-c35e-46f9-bceb-964d411d075f?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] items.
I was listening to latest episode [ https://substack.com/redirect/e7d9807d-b608-4824-83fb-51e4645a2f75?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] of WFMU’s Downtown Soulville when DJ Mr. Fine Wine described the CD he is offering as a premium for supporters of his show in the station’s current fund drive. The show features (often rare) soul and R&B on 45s, and so does the CD  — songs like “Doo Plus Two” by Dicky Doo and the Don’ts. Out of 25 songs on the disc, Fine Wine noted, Shazam (the popular song-identification app [ https://substack.com/redirect/530b437c-dbb3-4c5a-878a-bf704c913f97?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]) recognized only six or seven. The rest, he mused, were “unshazamable.” 
I liked this term, so I looked into it. Turns out that it’s been in use since at least the late 2010s, referring to music that Shazam doesn’t recognize and thus has a sort of “off the grid” connotation — and appeal.
This is partly a tribute to how astonishingly good Shazam is. I use it all the time [ https://substack.com/redirect/31b66810-69bc-4de9-9bb9-d3722c0760c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ], and I’m always surprised on those occasions when it’s stumped.
But that aside, maybe it’s also a handy term for something bigger. 
Everybody complains (understandably!) about the algorithms that shape our entertainment choices and direct our attention. But seeking the unshazmable isn’t just a way of escaping the algorithm. The unshazamable isn’t even in the database that the algorithm is designed to mine! 
Tapping into something enjoyable that didn’t come from a database doesn’t have to take the form of consuming a particular cultural object like a rare song; it could be an experience, a moment of presence. Looking at the moon can be unshazamable. 
So this week, be alert to, and try to appreciate, unshazamable things — in the broadest sense of the term!
THE HEARD
Sharing one randomly overheard song that I’ve enjoyed lately: Little unexpected bursts of delightful music are definitely things I savor [ https://substack.com/redirect/8a982640-718b-4599-a8fb-19d9054b6c4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ].
Speaking of WFMU (yes, I am a regular supporter), I was listening to Wreck Your Own Adventure [ https://substack.com/redirect/f78d294e-06ef-4b93-bba4-ddf024269b93?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] on the station’s Give the Drummer Radio [ https://substack.com/redirect/699bea0c-ec46-4e35-8653-f494cf616538?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] stream when “Sleep a Million Years,” by Kathy Heideman [ https://substack.com/redirect/dfcd5b2a-1038-422c-b785-46965cd273fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ], caught my ear. I had never heard of the singer, and I couldn’t place whether the song’s country/Americana sound was something contemporary or more vintage. I looked into it and found a couple [ https://substack.com/redirect/445c344b-1995-4aaa-9b1c-66a2e995955e?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] of articles [ https://substack.com/redirect/e4583529-c747-425b-a535-5146440ba662?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] that gave the back story, which turned out to be a great case study in open-earedness [ https://substack.com/redirect/66165b84-c35e-46f9-bceb-964d411d075f?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]. ...

subject: The Map That Shouldn’t Exist: When the Ice Vanished Before the Flood
body:
View this post on the web at https://markesecrets.substack.com/p/the-map-that-shouldnt-exist-when

Hello Friends! 
You know that feeling when you find a piece of the puzzle that doesn’t just go missing, it proves the entire picture on the box was a lie? That is where I am right now.
In 1929, in the archives of the Topkapi Palace in Istanbul, a fragment of a map drawn on gazelle skin was discovered. It is dated 1513, signed by the Ottoman Admiral Piri Reis. At first glance, it looks like a typical maritime map from the Age of Discovery. But as I’ve looked closer over the last few weeks, really looked, the foundations of our history began to shake.
A Mere Coincidence?
Academia will tell you that Piri Reis was simply a gifted compiler. He admitted himself that he based his map on over 20 older sources, including charts from the time of Alexander the Great. The official explanation is that the strange coastlines at the bottom of the map are a “fanciful” depiction of Terra Australis Incognita, the unknown southern land.
But here is the problem: the level of detail in the map matches the coastline of Queen Maud Land in Antarctica with terrifying accuracy.
The Hidden Truth Under the Ice
Here is what changes everything: The Piri Reis map shows Antarctica without ice. Modern science, including seismic surveys conducted by the British-Scandinavian Antarctic Expedition in 1949, confirms that the coastline Piri Reis drew in 1513 is the exact sub-glacial topography of the continent. This is what the land looks like under the ice.
The problem? Antarctica has been covered by a massive ice sheet for at least 6,000 years, some say millions. How could anyone map that coast with such precision before the ice formed? There is no official explanation that holds up. We are talking about cartographic knowledge that requires airborne surveying or advanced spherical trigonometry, thousands of years before the “Flood.”
The Red Thread
I see the pattern now. This isn’t an isolated incident. From the Sumerian King Lists to the mathematical perfection of the Mayan calendar, we are seeing the fingerprints of a lost, global civilization. A civilization that knew the true shape of the Earth and the movements of the stars long before we were “taught” how to write.
Think about Admiral Byrd and his “Operation Highjump.” Why was he so obsessed with Antarctica? What did he see down there that caused him to warn of a craft that could fly from pole to pole? I believe he found the remnants of the same source from which Piri Reis copied his maps. The Watchers, the Fallen, or those I call “The First,” they left a footprint that I am finally beginning to decode.
Do You Want to See Behind the Veil?
After spending years developing a system to separate disinformation from the actual “glimmers” of history, I don’t just look at the map; I look at the frequencies behind the information. It is a precise method of connecting archaeological finds with what I see unfolding in our world today.
The truth is out there, but it is locked behind layers of academic pride and deliberate obfuscation. I have decided not to just sharing what I find and instead start teaching you how I find it.
If you feel that something is missing in the story we’re being told, and you’re ready to stop being a passive reader and become an active seeker of the truth, I have laid out my roadmap for you.

This is the exact protocol I use to analyze declassified documents and ancient texts to find “The Red Thread” that connects our past to our present.

subject: Activate Your Heart Center
body:
View this post on the web at https://themindbodyspiritinstitute.substack.com/p/activate-your-heart-center

Welcome to Meditation Mondays! Every Monday, we will be uploading recordings from The Mind Body Spirit Institute’s free virtual meditation series: The Power of Community [ https://substack.com/redirect/46ad2202-97b3-48ce-a98f-5a000445f113?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]. Each week, a different MBSI instructor leads a guided 15-45 minute meditation via Zoom.
MBSI Director Jasmine Shah leads this week’s meditation, drawing from chakra healing practices in order to awaken and activate your heart center (or the heart chakra). Use sound and light visualization to take a moment to connect with your heart.
Register for The Power of Community (Spring 2026) [ https://substack.com/redirect/26e8f4e8-0e00-4170-94cd-256e37b973b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] today, and check out our full event calendar here [ https://substack.com/redirect/c2724264-4f1a-43c5-bfc3-0e7829eec424?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ], now with our spring schedule! This program is virtual, so you can join us for FREE from anywhere in the world.
If you enjoyed this meditation, please consider donating to The Mind Body Spirit Institute. Your generous contributions allow us to continue meeting our community's rising need for mental health support by funding MBSI's public programming [ https://substack.com/redirect/713f6383-b06f-4651-bbee-bbf05903f892?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] and consulting services [ https://substack.com/redirect/0c200b56-e041-4dce-afe4-8300ef530f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]. Thank you!
Jasmine Shah, MA, is the Director of The Jung Center’s Mind Body Spirit Institute. Jasmine holds an MA in Psychology with a focus on Spirituality, Mind, and Body Medicine from Columbia University, specializing in spirituality, consciousness, and transpersonal psychology. She works with organizations to help with workplace wellness and burnout through coaching and consulting, and continues to facilitate workshops in professional and private settings. She is passionate about restorative justice, and finds joy in writing poetry and dancing.

subject: NEMI ICB ANNOUNCEMENT
body:
In 2026, the sheet metal industry will convene under a new, unified conference model with the launch of the Sheet Metal Industry Institutes (SMII) Conference. For the first time, NEMI, the International Training Institute (ITI), and Sheet Metal Occupational Health Institute Trust (SMOHIT) will come together in a single, coordinated event, replacing the individual conferences previously held by each organization. This new structure reflects a deliberate effort to align education, training, certification, and workforce initiatives while providing industry leadership with a focused forum for collaboration and professional development. Attendees will have the opportunity to earn CEUs through the conference’s educational sessions to be used for the renewal of your ICB Certifications.

In support of this alignment, NEMI is working in coordination with the International Certification Board (ICB) on an updated approach to advanced professional certification delivery.

Beginning in 2026, the ICB NEMI Seminar and Certification Program will transition from a single annual conference‑based model to regionally delivered certification seminars, available to members from across the country. The three initial seminar locations will be intentionally selected in density‑rich markets where certification demand and workforce needs are the greatest. This ensures efficient access while maintaining the integrity and credibility of ICB/TABB credentials nationwide. It also allows members to attend the program location of their choice.

This program will launch the TABB Supervisor Seminar and Certification Exam, a four‑day instructional and examination event designed for experienced testing, adjusting, and balancing professionals who want to advance their supervisory responsibilities. The seminar integrates applied theory and hands‑on lab activities. Additional certification disciplines will be incorporated into the program as participation and industry demand continue to grow.

Stay tuned for additional information to come as the ICB NEMI Seminar and Certification Program schedule is created.

Meanwhile, registration for the SMII Conference is now open. Join NEMI, ITI, and SMOHIT September 22-24 in Atlanta. Register now at https://www.smiinst.org/conference/.

body:
View this post on the web at https://markesecrets.substack.com/p/beyond-the-narrative-the-search-for

What’s Next? Behind the Scenes of Our Discovery
I want to start by saying a sincere thank you. To those of you who have just joined us and to those who have been part of this journey from the beginning, and a special thanks to my Inner Circle Support. Your presence here is the fuel for everything I do. It is an incredible feeling to see our community grow so rapidly every single week. This isn’t just a hobby or a side project; this is a shared mission to reclaim a history that has been systematically obscured.
I appreciate you more than I can say. Because of your engagement and curiosity, I can dedicate my life to seeking a deeper truth, not just for myself, but for all of us. This is an ongoing process of disclosure, and right now, the trail is growing hotter than ever.
The Research is Accelerating
I am currently deep in the research phase for a major new article that I cannot wait to share with you. This piece focuses on the latest findings regarding architectural anomalies that defy conventional timelines, structures that suggest a level of precision and technology we are told did not exist thousands of years ago.
For those of you already in our member forum, you’ve likely seen the raw data and the preliminary observations I’ve been posting. The discussion there is already providing incredible insights, and I am working around the clock to weave these threads into a definitive breakdown for the main site. We are looking at a “Red Thread” that connects the high-altitude anomalies of the past to the modern-day “Breakaway Civilizations” that many are only just beginning to suspect exist.
Exploring the Archive: Our Four Essential Pillars
With the sheer volume of articles and research we have built, I want to ensure you have a clear map of our findings. If you are looking to understand the full scope of our work, I recommend starting with these four definitive volumes. Each one is a cornerstone of the Secret History mission:
The Foundations of Faith: The Sumerian Blueprint. Where do our traditions truly stem from? We trace the origins of modern theology back to the “Fallen Angels” and the Sumerian structures. This volume examines the Kajuna calendar and its connection to the Mayan systems, asking: was there once a singular, global influence that shaped humanity? Our Unique Heritage: The Bloodline Chronicles An investigation into our genetic markers and the historical lineages that suggest humanity is far more complex than evolutionary biology allows. We connect the Murung gods of South America to the elite structures of the ancient Near East.  [ https://substack.com/redirect/a52d4406-4e9c-47db-afbc-bfdad28ddc15?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]Access the Archive: [ https://substack.com/redirect/a52d4406-4e9c-47db-afbc-bfdad28ddc15?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]  [ https://substack.com/redirect/a52d4406-4e9c-47db-afbc-bfdad28ddc15?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]

subject: The Price of Complacency: A Call to Action for America
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-price-of-complacency-a-call-to

Many Americans are still trying to process the events that exposed the corruption and wickedness that have taken root in our country. People ask the question again and again: How did this happen?
There is an answer. But it is not one most people will like.
The answer is complacency.
It did not happen overnight. It did not come with tanks rolling down the streets or alarms warning of danger. It arrived quietly, patiently, while we were distracted.
When the internet arrived, something subtle began to change inside the American home. Families stopped sitting down together at the dinner table. Conversations were replaced with screens. Parents texted their children from the next room instead of speaking face to face. Meaningful human connection, physical touch, and genuine intimacy slowly gave way to endless scrolling, information overload, and digital drama.
Church attendance began to decline. PTA meetings became an inconvenience. Parent teacher conferences became optional. Many parents stopped asking their children about their day, and even fewer took the time to truly listen.
While we were busy, the system was waiting.
Once our guard was down, it moved in. Our children became the target. Schools that were once centers of learning slowly transformed into centers of ideological influence. Values that guided generations were quietly pushed aside and replaced with something entirely different.
The same pattern unfolded across the country.
In the 1980s, families began working multiple jobs just to stay afloat. Parents were exhausted. Time became scarce. While Americans were doing their best to provide for their families, changes were happening around them.
Prayer was removed from schools.
The Pledge of Allegiance was pushed aside.
The Ten Commandments were stripped from courthouses.
And what did the American people do?
Most went to work the next morning.
Children were dropped off at school or daycare.
Dry cleaning was picked up.
Groceries were bought.
Dinner was cooked.
The evening news played in the background.
Showers. Sleep.
Then the cycle began again the next day.
When changes began to appear in the interpretation and application of the Constitution, most Americans were too busy surviving to challenge it. When civic education began disappearing from school curriculum, few people noticed.
Why?
Because the system had already tested us.
Small compliance tests were introduced one after another. Each time the public accepted a little more, questioned a little less, and trusted a little too easily.
Eventually those in power understood something very clearly: the people were occupied with everything except watching them.
And in that vacuum, corruption flourished.
Government became filled with individuals who treated public service like personal opportunity. Predators found cover behind power. Career politicians traded loyalty to the nation for loyalty to donors, corporations, and foreign interests. Educated thieves learned how to manipulate systems designed to protect the people.
What should have been a house of representation became, in many places, a cesspool of corruption, arrogance, and moral decay.
But complacency did not stop with government.
It also reached into the world of media and influence.
In the modern age, many Americans place their trust in podcasters, commentators, and online influencers who claim to be speaking truth to power. Some of them built massive audiences because people believed they were independent voices standing up for the public.
But what happens when someone who gains that trust begins to go against the very principles they once claimed to defend?
Sometimes the reason is simple: money, attention, and influence.
Fear and outrage became profitable. Emotion became a commodity. Division became a marketing strategy.
Some voices discovered that keeping people angry or terrified generated more views, more clicks, more donations, and more subscribers. They capitalized on that fear and emotion, not caring whether it strengthened the country or tore it apart.
When influencers or podcasters preach nothing but hatred, division, or endless outrage, they are not strengthening the nation. They are feeding the same chaos that allowed corruption to grow in the first place.
The same responsibility that applies to politicians must apply to them as well.
If someone gains public trust and then betrays it, call them out.
Do not blindly follow personalities simply because they claim to be on your side. Do not allow anyone to manipulate your emotions for profit or influence.
If all a voice produces is anger, division, and contempt for fellow Americans, then that voice is not part of the solution. It is part of the problem.
In many ways, this culture of constant outrage is exactly why we ended up in the mess we see today.
A population that is constantly fighting itself is far easier to control.
And we see it even in small ways.
On our own YouTube channel, we often post prayers or encouraging poetry. We speak about hope, reflection, faith, and strengthening the spirit. And yet, sometimes we are called fake for doing so. Why? Because there exists a level of unfamiliar depth that challenges the attitudes people have grown comfortable with.
We do not have one hundred thousand subscribers.
We do not have seventy five thousand.
We do not even have five thousand.
And that says something about the environment we are living in.
People would rather tune in and hear the same drama repeated for nearly ten years. The same outrage cycles. The same rumors. The same endless speculation.
A prayer invoking the name of God is suddenly considered offensive. Meanwhile, thousands will rush to another channel to see if some grotesque file connected to Epstein has been released.
Can you see the contradiction?
Content that uplifts the spirit is mocked. Content that feeds darkness, scandal, and obsession is consumed endlessly.
This is exactly how attention gets manipulated.
A distracted population is easier to steer. A divided population is easier to control. A spiritually empty population is easier to influence.
But none of this is irreversible.
This is not about blaming people for being busy, tired, or overwhelmed. Most Americans have been working hard just to build a life for their families.
This is about recognizing what happened and choosing to change course.
Turn off the noise once in a while.
Sit down at the dinner table again.
Ask your children about their day and truly listen.
Attend the school meetings.
Learn the Constitution.
Research the people who ask for your vote.
And hold accountable every voice that tries to manipulate the public, whether they sit in government offices or behind microphones and cameras.
Community begins at home. Accountability begins with citizens.
Most importantly, restore the moral and spiritual foundation that built this nation in the first place. A country cannot remove its moral compass and expect to maintain its direction.
America was never meant to be sustained by government alone. It was meant to be sustained by families, faith, responsibility, and active citizens.
The system only gained power when the people stepped away.
Now the question before us is simple.
Will we remain distracted, or will we step back in?
The future of this nation will not be decided by politicians alone. It will be decided by whether ordinary Americans choose to wake up, reengage, and reclaim the responsibility that comes with freedom.
The call to action has already been issued.
The only question left is whether the people will answer it.

Caption: 

👋 I’m [Justin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justincharlesgordon/). I run The SF Grind, [The LA Grind](https://www.thelagrind.com/), and scout for [Headline](https://headline.com/). I live in LA but spend a lot of time in San Francisco meeting founders, hosting gatherings, and enjoying the wonderful city.

**Happy Monday!** I've been getting a ton of questions lately about how I use events to grow and monetize The LA Grind and The SF Grind, so I'm running a workshop.

Over the last 10 months I've crossed $100K in revenue, driven mostly by events. I've hosted 50+ events, big and small, across LA and SF. I’ve figured out what works, what doesn't, and what moves the needle.

In this 90-minute virtual session I'll cover everything: how to structure events, handle RSVPs, manage operations, land sponsors, what to charge them, and more. Real numbers, screenshots, and I'll answer every question you have.

This is for newsletter operators, founders, business owners, and GTM leaders who want to use events as a growth and revenue channel.

It’s happening on **Tuesday, April 7th from 8 to 9:30 am PT**. Cost is $499.

[Grab your spot here. ](https://buy.stripe.com/5kQeVefkg4hTaNeb6efbq0q)

Let’s get to it.
