  /*
      ------------------------------------
      EMAIL TABLE STYLES
      ------------------------------------
      - Cannot use position absolutes
      - Cannot use margin-top negative
  */

  /**UTILITY*/
  [data-ui-clearfix] {
      clear: both;
  }
  [data-ui-spacer] {
      height: 20px;
  }
  [data-ui-borders] {
    border: 1px solid #e6e6e6;
  }
  table[data-ui-wrap-parent],
  .tbl[data-ui-wrap-parent] {
    /*NOTE: This is necessary for word wraps and
     *      breaks to take effect on children
     *      elements. Use this for tables tags.
     *      Create new selectors for divs with
     *      receiving display:table, use .tbl
     *      consistently to avoid ever growing
     *      one off selectors*/
    table-layout: fixed;
  }
  div[data-ui-wrap-longword] {
      /*NOTE: Allow break on long words w/o spaces*/
      /*NOTE: Make sure to add this attributes on a div
       *      with a td parent*/
      /*NOTE: Finding that overflow-wrap: break-word;
       *      accomplishes the same thing as
       *      word-wrap: break-word; on Firefox and
       *      Chrome*/
      /*NOTE: Finding that word-break: break-word;
      /*      is not doing anything???*/
      /*NOTE: On some browsers this does not work
       *      by itself must be combined with
       *      word-break: break-word*/

      /*NOTE: Firefox, Chrome, Safari*/
      word-wrap: break-word;

      /*NOTE: IE11*/
      -ms-word-wrap: break-word;

  }

  /**OVERRIDE OUTLOOK*/
  .EmailClientBody {
    mso-line-height-rule:exactly;
  }

  /**EMAIL OUTER FILL*/
    .EmailOuterFill-inner {
      background: #F7F8F9;
      /* NOTE: 5% side paddings are intentional
       *       email will be difficult to read on
       *       mobile or narrow screens if we go
       *       with something like 40px*/
      padding: 20px 5% 0;
    }

  /**EMAIL OUTER*/
    .EmailSection-outer {
      background: #fff;
      margin-top: 20px;
    }
    .EmailOuterPage-outer {
      max-width: 720px;
      margin: 0 auto;
    }
    .EmailOuterPage-outer[data-ui-template="basic"] {
      max-width: 600px;
    }

  /**EMAIL HEADER*/
    .EmailTop {
      text-align: center;
      padding: 20px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
    }
    .EmailTop__text {
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
    }

  /**EMAIL HEADER BAR*/
    .Email-HeaderBar-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-HeaderBar-inner {
      border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0;
      border-color: #000000;
      border-bottom: none;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 30px;
      text-align: center;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }

  /**EMAIL BANNER*/
    .Email-Banner-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-Banner-inner {
      border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0;
      border-color: #000000;
      border-bottom: none;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 20px;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }

  /**EMAIL SECTION HEADER*/
    .Email-SectionHeader {
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 20px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text {
      line-height: 1.4;
      margin-top: 5px;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text-main {
      font-size: 18px;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text-sub {
      color: #888F9F;
      font-size: 14px;
      font-weight: normal;
    }

  /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT*/
    .Email-SectionContent {
      color: #1F232F;
      font-size: 20px;
    }
    .Email-SectionContent-inner {
      padding: 20px 30px 30px
    }
    .Email-SectionContent__body .Email-SectionContent__body-text {
      margin-top: 0;
      margin-bottom: 10px;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT STRIPE*/
    .Email-SectionContentStripe {
      color: #1F232F;
    }
    .Email-SectionContentStripe-inner {
      padding: 20px;
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-SectionContentStripe__text {
      word-break: break-word;
      overflow-wrap: break-word;
      line-height: 1.4;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT - SUB BODY*/
    .Email-SectionContent__sub-body {
      font-size: 16px;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION FOOTNOTE*/
    .Email-SectionFootnote-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-inner {
      border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px;
      padding: 10px 20px;
      background-color: #e0e0e0;
      color: #8a8a8a;
      line-height: 1.4;
      border-top: 1px solid #dcdcdc;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote--footer .Email-SectionFootnote-inner {
      padding: 20px 30px;
      text-align: center;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-item {
      margin: 0 10px;
      display: inline-block;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-item a {
      color: #8a8a8a;
      text-decoration: underline;
    }
  /**EMAIL ACTIONS*/
    .Email-Actions-inner {
      /*NOTE: bottom padding takes account for bottom
        margin applied to children buttons*/
      padding: 10px 20px 10px;
      border-top: none;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-Actions [data-ui-div-whitespace] {
      /*NOTE: This is whitespace adjustment that
       *      that will be ignored by Outlook on
       *      client/Windows*/
      /*NOTE: bottom padding takes account for bottom
        margin applied to children buttons*/
      padding-bottom: 10px;
    }
    .Email-Actions .Email-ActionButton__span {
      /*NOTE: This element and/or styles prevent
       *      buttons from being 100% width and
       *      allows buttons to wrap.
       *      These styles will be ignored by Outlook
       *      (client/Windows).
       *      In Outlook (client/Windows), this element
       *      will behave like inline block.*/
      margin-right: 10px;
      display: block;
      float: left;
    }
    .Email-Actions .Email-ActionButton__a {
      margin-top: 10px;
      display: block;
      color: #fff;
      text-decoration: none;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: .12em;

    .EmailBtm {

subject: AI Money is coming to a midterm near you
body:
In one North Carolina district they already dropped more than half a million dollars on one primary ad.

Hi Joshua willems, it’s Faiz from More Perfect Union.

The massive AI company Anthropic is behind more than a half a million dollars in ads in one North Carolina district. Already.

That’s right, the spending for and against candidates based on who billion dollar Big Tech companies think will get them the biggest bang for their buck has already begun.

Bernie Sanders-backed Nida Allam supports a nationwide AI data center moratorium. Incumbent Valerie Foushee sits on a new AI committee in congress, won’t stand up to data centers, and she won’t commit to not taking AI money. In fact, when asked whether she would reject AI industry money by students at a forum, Foushee actually ran away.

Watch our exclusive report exposing how Anthropic and the rest of Big Tech are just getting started now.

WATCH & SHARE

Anthropic has put up $20 million to spend on the 2026 midterms, but of course, they aren’t alone.

Executives from Open AI and Palantir will spend over $100 million on the upcoming midterm election.

Meta is spending at least $65 million dollars.

Big tech companies and their CEOs are funneling all this money into super PACs, non-profits, and dark money groups. Their goal is simple: Elect candidates who will let AI companies do what they want. More unregulated development of AI, more data centers, more layoffs.

Check out the report and then share it on social, because everyone needs to know why Big Tech is terrified of Nida Allam.

In solidarity,

-Faiz

Faiz Shakir, Co-Founder
More Perfect Union

subject: The Last Prophesy
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-last-prophesy

There has always been a final warning before a great turning point in history. Civilizations rise in brilliance and power, then decay in pride and corruption. Prophets speak, are mocked, and are remembered only after the collapse. The pattern is ancient. The pattern is undeniable. The question is not whether there will be a last prophesy. The question is whether we are living inside it now.
From the days of Book of Daniel to the visions recorded in Book of Revelation, humanity has been warned that empires built on injustice eventually fall. These writings describe kingdoms that devour the weak, systems that mark and track populations, and rulers who exalt themselves as saviors while demanding obedience. They speak of deception so powerful that many accept it as truth.
The last prophesy is not merely about fire from the sky or armies crossing borders. It is about moral inversion. It is about a world where good is labeled evil and evil is celebrated as progress. It is about confusion intentionally manufactured to weaken discernment. When truth becomes negotiable and conscience is mocked, the stage is set for judgment.
Throughout history, leaders have sought to centralize power. In ancient Rome, citizens traded liberty for security. In medieval kingdoms, crowns ruled with divine claims. In modern times, technology has achieved what no emperor could accomplish. Surveillance is instant. Communication is global. Influence is invisible yet constant. The infrastructure now exists for control on a scale once thought impossible.
The last prophesy warns of unity without righteousness. It warns of peace built on compromise with corruption. It warns of systems that promise safety while quietly demanding allegiance. The danger is not always force. Often it is comfort. Often it is convenience. Often it is fear.
Consider how quickly societies shift during crisis. Rights once considered permanent can be suspended. Speech can be filtered. Movement can be restricted. Those who question the narrative can be labeled dangerous. History shows that fear is the most effective tool for reshaping a population. When people are afraid, they surrender freedoms they would otherwise defend.
The prophetic texts also speak of a remnant. A small group who refuse to bow. They are not perfect, but they are steadfast. They measure events against eternal principles rather than temporary trends. They understand that truth does not change with opinion polls.
The final warning is spiritual before it is political. It addresses the condition of the human heart. Pride precedes destruction. Greed corrodes judgment. Power without humility becomes tyranny. The last prophesy calls individuals to examine themselves before condemning nations.
Many search for dates and timelines. They analyze symbols and calculate years. Yet the deeper message is not a calendar. It is a choice. Every generation faces the decision to align with truth or to follow deception. Every generation believes it is more advanced than the last, yet the fundamental struggle remains the same.
If this is the era of the last prophesy, then it will not unfold only in grand events. It will unfold in daily decisions. It will unfold in whether people speak truth when silence is safer. It will unfold in whether families teach discernment or outsource morality to institutions. It will unfold in whether courage outweighs comfort.
The signs described in ancient scripture were not meant to create panic. They were meant to awaken vigilance. They were meant to remind humanity that history is not random. Actions have consequences. Justice may be delayed, but it is not denied.
The last prophesy is both a warning and an invitation. A warning that unchecked corruption collapses under its own weight. An invitation to stand firm when deception grows louder. It is not merely about the end of an age. It is about the revealing of hearts.
Whether one views prophecy through faith or skepticism, the pattern remains clear. When truth erodes and power concentrates without accountability, societies tremble. When conscience is silenced, chaos follows. The final chapter of any civilization is written not only by its rulers, but by its people.
The last prophesy may not be a single event shouted from the sky. It may be a whisper growing louder in the conscience of humanity. A call to wakefulness. A call to courage. A call to remember that no system, no empire, and no deception lasts forever.
In the end, the final warning is simple. Choose wisely. Stand firmly. And understand that history always answers the question of who listened and who refused.

subject: "Attention is the New Time"
body:
View this post on the web at https://jeremydjohnson.substack.com/p/attention-is-the-new-time

Dear readers,
It has been a minute. I know. Teaching online courses can often be intensifying in an inward-bound way. There’s a rhythm to it, of course. Deep inhalation before the exhale. Tonight is the final lecture of my annual course teaching Jean Gebser’s book, The Ever-Present Origin (1949), and so I feel that exhalation coming. With it, I feel a renewed sense of inspiration. I’m in the final few weeks of editing the new manuscript (working in reverse, from back to front), and feel like there’s just so much to write about here, in the Mutations project, and more discussions to be scheduled through the podcast.
Over the weekend, I hosted a conversation and community discussion with Cynthia Bourgeault. It began as an ‘office hours’ for the students but quickly morphed into something of a gathering place, a middle, for our mutual communities to have an enlivening discussion on “the Gebserian take [ https://open.substack.com/pub/cynthiabourgeault/p/the-gebserian-take?utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web ].” Not just about what was said in Bourgeault’s article, but about the kind of wisdom and insight that might be drawn from reading Gebser in a time of civilizational transition. What constitutes living through a time of collapse and worldview shift? How do we tend to- and witness the structure of consciousness (Gebser’s terminology) that is dying, and what is ours to contribute to the emergence of the new mutation? How do we live the new in such times?
I think, for me, the most memorable takeaway was Bourgeault’s statement with regards to the new worldview, which Gebser emphasizes is temporal in nature. Bourgeault says that “attention is the new time.” This, to me, feels deeply aligned with the themes I presented during last December’s “integral futuring” course. 
There is a kind of radical and transformative emphasis in Gebser’s work that might be overlooked here, much as our culture of hyper-productivity tends overlook the present: the way we reclaim time from the foreclosure of the future (i.e., from neoliberal, or capital time) is through reclaiming the weird time of the present. Presence ripens things, as Rilke knew. It is in the present that past and future are in attendance, and as Bourgeault states, attention is the new time. Whatever futures lie beyond progress and its shadow-side, catastrophe, they will only have their chance if we succeed in living them, that is, attending to them as conscious present.
“Attention is the new time.”
After discussing it, Bourgeault and I wanted to make this discussion available for our mutual communities, and for the larger public. It is, I hope, the first in a series of conversations, and feels like it sets a resonant tone for the Mutations podcast this year.

I love the spirit of offering up far-flung explorations in such a leisurely, unpackaged way — even as I’m hesitant about adding to my screen time.

subject: A letter from our CEO
body:
CustomInk.com - Our commitment to showing up for you.

Hi there,

As one of our most important customers, you know that a custom hoodie or a branded tumbler is never just "stuff." It's how you build your brand, recognize employees, acquire and retain customers, and set your teams up for success. For 25 years, we’ve been the company you trust to help you get custom t-shirts to drive that success. Today, we are excited to share the next chapter of that story. We’re refreshing our brand, and our new mantra is simple: Ink Is More Than You Think. 

Read More
(https://blog.customink.com/brand-update/)

More Than Just a Fresh Coat of Paint
This isn't just a new tagline. Over the last 18 months, we’ve made massive investments to make your job easier:
- Expanded Catalog: Over 10,000 products, including premium brands like YETI, Adidas, Nike, and The North Face across apparel, accessories, and promo products.
- Low Minimums: You can now order single samples of over 1,000 products to see and feel the quality before committing your budget.
- Better Service: We’ve restructured our team to provide dedicated account management and specialists for teams of every size.
And so much more!

What’s Not Changing
The "Inkers" who pick up the phone and genuinely care about your order aren't going anywhere. Our Design Lab remains the easiest way to create, and our guarantee remains the same: no unhappy surprises. Swag is rarely anyone’s full-time job, but everyone notices when it’s done right. 

That’s the promise behind “Ink Is More Than You Think.” It’s our commitment to showing up for you, whether you’re ordering for 10 people or 10,000.

Thank you for being part of our story. We can’t wait to show you what’s next.

Best,

David Doctorow
CEO, Custom Ink

===================================================================

CONTACT US

800-293-4232
service@customink.com

===================================================================

please add service@customink.com to your email address book or contact list.

subject: The Luciferians Are Pushing Time Toward Armageddon
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-luciferians-are-pushing-time

There is a growing conviction among researchers, theologians, and independent analysts that powerful Luciferian forces are actively accelerating humanity toward Armageddon. This is not framed as random chaos or accidental decline. It is seen as intentional orchestration. A deliberate tightening of global pressure designed to force prophetic timelines into fulfillment.
Armageddon, as described in the Book of Revelation, is the final confrontation between light and darkness. It is the culmination of corruption, deception, and concentrated power rising against divine order. Those who believe Luciferians are steering world events argue that what we are witnessing today mirrors that trajectory with startling precision.
Strategic Acceleration
The acceleration is visible in multiple arenas at once.
Geopolitical tensions are escalating rather than cooling. Regional conflicts are entangled into broader alliances. Economic systems are consolidating into fewer hands. Surveillance technologies expand under the banner of security. Cultural foundations are destabilized through engineered division.
This is not random fragmentation. It is structured destabilization.
Luciferian philosophy, as understood by its critics, centers on rebellion against divine authority, the exaltation of human will, and the pursuit of hidden knowledge as power. If such ideology exists within elite circles, its natural outcome would be global transformation through crisis. Crisis becomes the catalyst. Collapse becomes the doorway.
Manufactured Chaos
The pattern follows a recognizable formula:
Create instability
Amplify fear
Offer centralized control as the solution
Economic shocks justify financial restructuring. Security threats justify mass surveillance. Social unrest justifies expanded state power. Each crisis moves the world closer to unified systems of governance and digital oversight.
From this perspective, Armageddon is not merely a battlefield. It is a systemic convergence point where political, spiritual, and technological forces merge into a final confrontation.
Spiritual Symbolism Made Physical
The term Luciferian does not merely describe an occult practice. It represents a worldview that elevates enlightenment through defiance. In this framework, pushing humanity toward a climactic global event would be consistent with a desire to dethrone divine order and replace it with human engineered sovereignty.
Critics argue that symbols long associated with occult traditions appear within elite institutions, media, architecture, and ceremonies. Whether symbolic or literal, the repetition reinforces the belief that spiritual ideology influences policy and power.
Armageddon, then, is not chaos for chaos’ sake. It is transformation through fire. A forced reset. A breaking down of existing systems to erect something new.
Time Compression
One of the most striking elements is the sense of time compression. Technological advancement has shrunk decades of change into years. Artificial intelligence reshapes labor. Digital currency restructures finance. Information warfare manipulates perception at scale.
This rapid acceleration mirrors prophetic language describing birth pains increasing in frequency and intensity. The world does not drift toward crisis. It sprints.
Those who hold the affirmative view argue that this sprint is engineered.
The Endgame
What would pushing time to Armageddon accomplish?
Total consolidation of power
Spiritual inversion of moral order
A final test of allegiance
In apocalyptic theology, the climax separates loyalty from compromise. If one believes Luciferians seek ultimate control, accelerating humanity into such a crossroads would serve that objective.
Last Words
The assertion is clear. The acceleration of global instability is not accidental. The convergence of political centralization, technological dominance, and moral upheaval reflects a coordinated trajectory.
Armageddon is not merely awaited. It is being advanced.
Whether one interprets this through theology, symbolism, or geopolitical analysis, the pattern appears deliberate. The world is not simply unraveling. It is being steered toward a decisive reckoning.

subject: DCF/DHS and Legal Hierarchy
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/dcfdhs-and-legal-hierarchy

In an age where nearly every driveway, porch, and doorway is monitored by a camera, a troubling question arises. Why, in a court of law, does sworn testimony sometimes outweigh verifiable digital evidence?
Across the country, agencies such as the Florida Department of Children and Families and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services operate under statutory authority intended to protect vulnerable children. Their mandate is serious. Their role is powerful. Their word carries weight in courtrooms that make life altering decisions about families every day.
But what happens when that weight becomes imbalance?
Doorbell systems produced by companies like Ring and other security platforms record around the clock. Neighbors record. Streets record. Businesses record. Many homes maintain documented proof of who arrived and who did not on any given date and time.
Yet there have been instances in which case workers or investigators report to a court that they attempted a court ordered home visit or wellness check and the subject was not present. Based on that report alone, the court may find the party in contempt. When the accused individual appears before a judge and requests verification of the specific date and time, offering security footage that covers a twelve or twenty four hour window, they are sometimes told the court has no means to view the footage or that it cannot be admitted. In these moments, the sworn statement of the agency representative is placed above the tangible evidence offered by the citizen standing before the bench.
This raises a fundamental concern about legal hierarchy. Is the word of an agency representative automatically elevated above verifiable digital evidence. Should it be.
Courts rely heavily on sworn testimony. Judges must assess credibility and make determinations quickly, often under intense pressure. However, in a digital era where objective evidence can be produced within minutes, it is reasonable to ask whether such evidence should at least be reviewed before a person is found in contempt of court.
The issue is not whether agencies should be trusted. The issue is whether evidence should be equally considered regardless of its source.
In Florida, a neighbor reported alleged sexual misconduct involving children and deplorable housing conditions. The report was submitted through an online system that required the reporting party to provide a real name and email address, even though the disclaimer stated that only a supervisor would retain that identifying information. The notice further indicated that the information would not be disclosed to the assigned case officer and that if clarification were needed, a supervisor would make contact.
A case officer later arrived at the residence, spoke to the parents outside for approximately five minutes, did not enter the home, and concluded the visit. Afterward, the reporting party’s email address, including their last name, was disclosed to the subjects of the complaint.
This situation presents serious concerns regarding confidentiality, procedure, and safety. If a system promises anonymity beyond supervisory review, the disclosure of identifying information undermines trust in the reporting structure. If allegations include deplorable housing conditions, a failure to conduct an interior inspection raises questions about the thoroughness of the investigation. When identifying information is released in sensitive cases, the reporting party may be exposed to retaliation.
Family courts often operate on expedited timelines. Judges manage heavy dockets and depend on agency reports when making decisions about custody, visitation, and parental rights. Reliance on agency documentation is understandable. However, reliance can shift into deference when agency testimony is treated as presumptively superior to all other forms of proof.
The structural concern is straightforward. Who verifies the verifier. What recourse exists when procedures are not followed. What standard governs the admission of readily available digital evidence.
There is also a broader national concern that cannot be ignored. It is now publicly documented through federal oversight reviews that thousands of unaccompanied migrant children who crossed the southern border were released to sponsors and that federal tracking and follow up processes faced significant gaps. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services through its Office of Refugee Resettlement has faced scrutiny regarding incomplete documentation and limited post release follow up in certain cases. When agencies tasked with child welfare struggle with consistent record keeping and oversight, public confidence is strained.
If deficiencies in tracking and accountability can occur at a federal level involving vulnerable children, citizens are justified in demanding higher transparency and stronger safeguards at every level of the system.
This is not an indictment of every social worker, judge, or attorney. Many enter their professions with integrity and a sincere desire to serve. The concern is systemic. Authority must be balanced with oversight. Credibility must be paired with accountability. Constitutional rights must not be treated as secondary to administrative convenience.
There are those who argue that court reform will never occur because the problems are too entrenched and too widespread. Whether one agrees or disagrees with that view, the frustration reflects a deeper issue. Trust in institutions declines when citizens believe there is no meaningful remedy for misconduct or constitutional infringement.
If the system is to endure, it must recommit to foundational principles. Equal protection under the law. Due process. Transparent procedures. Admissibility of relevant evidence. Clear consequences when officials violate rights under color of law.
Restoring confidence does not require dismantling the republic. It requires returning to it. It requires enforcing constitutional limits on government authority and holding judges, attorneys, prosecutors, and law enforcement officers accountable through lawful oversight mechanisms when they infringe upon the rights of citizens.
The path forward must remain constitutional, peaceful, and grounded in the rule of law. Without accountability, authority loses legitimacy. Without legitimacy, trust dissolves.
Children deserve protection. Families deserve fairness. Reporters deserve confidentiality. Citizens deserve their constitutional rights.
If justice is to mean anything, it must apply evenly, regardless of title, position, or badge.

subject: [PODCAST #629] 👉 Shadow, Stress, and Perceiving Functions (Listener Q&A)
body:
Is your “shadow” running the show when you’re stressed?
 

"Make Your Arguments Bulletproof"

Live Workshop, Saturday, March 7 — Join Us
 

Hi Joshua,

 

Personality typing can feel like the wild west right now... tons of opinions, loud certainty, and not enough real-world observation.

 

And when you understand how your mind actually works under stress, the chaos starts to organize itself.

In this week’s episode we respond to listener questions that hit where it matters most: how cognitive functions show up in real life, especially when you’re anxious, overthinking, or unsure of yourself.
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕
 

Can We Get Your Advice?
Antonia and I are shaping the podcast for the coming season and we’d love your input & advice. We created a quick 2-minute check-in to learn what you actually need right now. Your guidance will help us build the most relevant tools and topics over the next few weeks.

👉 Share Your Advice » (2 min)
 

In this episode, we explore:

  • Why perceiving doesn’t mean passive, and how Extraverted Sensing (Se) can look “action-oriented” because it gathers information through direct engagement with the environment.

  • The difference between Se direct responsiveness and Te systems-and-structure approach to getting things done.

  • What “wisdom” really is, and why it’s less about abstract truth and more about applied experience and discernment.

  • How shadow functions can follow the same certainty/uncertainty pattern as your primary functions, while staying mostly unconscious until pressure reveals them.

  • What happens when your environment suppresses your natural wiring, and how those parts still find a way to grow.

👉 We’d love to hear from you: When you’re stressed, what pattern do you notice yourself repeating most?

<— Hit reply and share your experience with us.

 

We released this podcast in both video and audio this week.
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕
 


Much Love,

Joel Mark Witt & Antonia Dodge
Co-Founders | Personality Hacker
 

PS - Make Your Arguments Bulletproof

Antonia is hosting a live workshop on March 7th teaching her 7-step system to refine any belief to precision. This is the exact process she used to reprogram her own mind after leaving a cult.

And it's one of the core skills of Introverted Thinking.
Make Your Arguments Bulletproof ⮕

subject: [Care Ministry: Prayer Sheet] TLC Prayer Sheet 2/24
body:
TLC Prayer Sheet 2/24

Remember in school you'd be writing a paper, or working on a
presentation, or doing some sort of book study and you'd have to
come up with or find a theme? Sometimes there was a clear theme,
sometimes you had to stretch a little, but either way it was
mostly just to check a box, and be on your way.

We don't necessarily think about themes in our everyday life.

The hymn "There is a Fountain" has a line, "redeeming love has
been my theme" and I think that pretty much sums up the truest
and most beautiful theme we can have as Christians.

Here's that specific verse

Ever since, by faith, I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die:
And shall be till I die,
And shall be till I die;
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.

And if you want to give it a listen, click here. 
( https://youtu.be/QF8sPZmP8fU?si=3njtg8ao21bwXGG7 )

But whether you listen or not, consider writing the truth of
Christ's redeeming love on the tablet of your heart, and letting
it be the anthem of your soul.

subject: Before Trump’s State of the Unionaddress…
body:
Joshua willems,

Last Friday, the Supreme Court ruled that Donald Trump had instituted an illegal tariff regime, resulting in more than $200 billion in arbitrarily higher prices over the last year.

Businesses like Costco, FedEx, Crocs, and Revlon have filed lawsuits demanding refunds from the federal government. But those companies already passed higher prices along to their customers. Instead of giving hundreds of billions more to corporations who are already benefiting from Trump’s massive tax cuts, those refunds should go to the working families who have been paying higher prices.

Let’s do the math:

The U.S. Department of Treasury says that Trump’s illegal tariffs brought in $223 billion since they were instituted.

There are 134.8 million households in the United States.

That means that on average, each family paid an extra $1,654.30!

Sign the petition to demand a $1,700 tariff rebate check before Trump begins his State of the Union address!

DEMAND A REFUND

In solidarity,

-Faiz

Faiz Shakir, Co-Founder

Lacy Warne is a Licensed Therapist (https://www.lacywarne.com/) with over 14 years of experience and a thriving private practice in Santa Cruz, CA, specializing in anxiety disorders and EMDR to help clients find deep, lasting relief. She is a wife and momma to two wonderful littles.

Through every act, Jesus showed us a love that is constant, sacrificial, and beyond measure.

subject: How to Save the Media
body:
View this post on the web at https://post.substack.com/p/how-to-save-the-media

I’m writing a book about the state of the media that will be published later this year. It’s called How to Save the Media. You can pre-order it here:
It’s a bold title, I know. But there’s little doubt that the media is in crisis. Even as it seems that more news is being consumed than ever, it hardly feels like we’re getting smarter. Mad kings rule the media economy and reap the rewards. News organizations are doing mass layoffs. Impartial reporting is out; jestergooning is in.
But I believe there’s reason to hope. I’ve seen what can happen when publishers take ownership and audiences directly support the work they believe in. I’ve seen a new media market grow from nothing and watched once-struggling writers find financial security. I’ve seen them build new institutions, giving rise to a generation of fresh voices. And I’ve seen audiences vote for the culture they want to see, funding the voices and perspectives they value—leading to more than 5 million paid subscriptions on this platform alone.
So I’m capturing this pivotal time in the pages of a book.
How to Save the Media is about this era of transition, where old gatekeepers give way to new opportunities and direct relationships reign supreme. It’s about an emerging ecosystem where success doesn’t have to depend on who you know or how well you cater to an algorithm. It shows a way to recover from the collapse of traditional media, and escape the deranging effects of the attention economy.
This book tackles the biggest questions facing the media and society, from how to protect the free press to how to resist a robot uprising, taking readers into rooms with some of the biggest media power players of our time, including berserk billionaires and heroic hacks. I’ll blend insider access with outsider perspective, drawing on my history in media and tech across two decades and three continents, from scrabbling freelance journalist to co-founder of Substack. You’ll see how we got here and where we’re going next—from the temple to the garden [ https://substack.com/redirect/3d414707-5de7-4b5e-9d7e-fc1b26e8e4c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ].
How to Save the Media will be published by Authors Equity, a new publishing company that practices what this book preaches: authors retain full ownership of their work and receive the majority of the sales revenue. The cover art is by my exceptional colleague Joro Chen.
Pre-orders are available now. They matter more than many people realize; they’re what determine whether a book breaks through and reaches a wider audience. So consider pre-ordering if you believe in a different future for media: one where creators own their work, audiences help shape the culture they want to thrive, and power flows to people rather than platforms. This is about saving the media—but also about making it better than it’s ever been.

subject:
Pedophiles and How They Have Walked Among Us and Multiplied Using Symbols and
 Codes
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/pedophiles-and-how-they-have-walked

Evil rarely announces itself.
It does not wear a label. It does not carry a sign. It blends. It adapts. It studies culture and learns how to survive within it.
Throughout history, those who prey on children have understood one core principle. Survival depends on recognition without exposure. To operate, they must be able to identify one another while remaining invisible to everyone else.
This is where codes and symbols enter the picture.
Human beings have always used symbols to signal belonging. From ancient guilds to secret societies, from underground movements to resistance groups, coded imagery and layered language have allowed people to communicate quietly within larger populations. Predators exploit the same psychological mechanism.
A symbol on its own means nothing. Context gives it power. Within a closed circle, a shape, phrase, or subtle reference can serve as a signal. Outside that circle, it appears ordinary.
This dual meaning creates safety for those who use it.
Predators often test language before trust. A phrase with unusual emphasis. A joke that crosses a line but is disguised as humor. A shared reference to something inappropriate framed as irony. If the other person recoils, it was just a joke. If the other person responds in kind, a door quietly opens.
Codes do not have to be dramatic. They can be numbers embedded in usernames. Repeated patterns. Certain combinations of letters. Specific terminology that only makes sense inside a closed conversation. In the digital age, encrypted communication and niche online spaces amplify this effect, allowing like minded individuals to find one another across continents without public visibility.
Multiplication does not happen because of symbols alone.
It happens because silence protects them.
When communities avoid difficult conversations, predators gain cover. When warning signs are dismissed as imagination, manipulation thrives. When people are more concerned with comfort than confrontation, exploitation spreads.
Predators often operate through grooming long before abuse occurs. Grooming is itself a coded process. Gradual boundary shifts. Secrecy disguised as special attention. Isolation framed as mentorship. Each step small enough to avoid alarm, but intentional enough to create control.
In this sense, the greatest symbol predators rely on is not a graphic mark or hidden emblem. It is normalcy.
They look ordinary.
They sound ordinary.
They participate in ordinary life.
Because they appear familiar, suspicion feels uncomfortable.
Multiplication happens when networks validate behavior instead of challenging it. When deviance is normalized within private circles. When technology removes geographic limits. When anonymity reduces consequence.
Symbols and codes are tools. Silence is fertilizer.
The reality is sobering. The threat has never been mythical creatures hiding in caves. It has been individuals who understand psychology, leverage trust, and recognize one another through subtle signals most people overlook.
Awareness does not require paranoia. It requires discernment.
The way forward is not obsessive decoding of every image or word. It is vigilance in behavior. It is teaching children boundaries. It is empowering them to speak without fear. It is adults refusing to ignore intuition when something feels wrong.
Predators survive through secrecy.
They multiply through silence.
They hide through familiarity.
They walk among us not because they are invisible,
but because too often,
no one wants to see.

subject: Deception from the Least Likely Places
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/deception-from-the-least-likely-places

For a Friend 
Deception rarely arrives wearing a warning label. It does not usually come from declared enemies or obvious liars. It slips in quietly. It smiles across the table. It holds your hand. It builds routines with you. It becomes normal.
That is what makes it so disorienting.
You meet someone steady. Consistent. Predictable in the best way. The morning texts arrive like clockwork. The phone calls stretch late into the night. Plans are made. Inside jokes are born. The rhythm of two lives begins to synchronize. There is no chaos. No red flags waving wildly in the wind. Just a gradual weaving together of time and trust.
Normalcy is powerful. It lowers defenses without asking permission.
Then something shifts.
The calls change. They are shorter. Less frequent. The tone is different. Emails become delayed or oddly formal. Text messages that once carried warmth now feel mechanical. There are explanations. They did not feel good. They have a lot going on. Work is overwhelming. Family needs attention. Life is complicated.
Individually, those reasons are reasonable. Adults have responsibilities. People get sick. Stress happens. That is why deception hides there. It borrows believable circumstances and stands behind them.
The issue is not always that someone has moved on. People fall out of love. Interests change. Priorities shift. That is painful, yes, but it is human. The deeper sting comes from something else.
It comes from the quiet rewriting of reality.
It is when patterns are denied. When obvious distance is treated as imagination. When your intuition is subtly dismissed. You notice the change, but you are told nothing has changed. You feel the withdrawal, but you are reassured that everything is fine. You see the fading effort, yet you are asked to ignore it.
That is not heartbreak. That is insult.
Because the unspoken message is this: you will not notice. You will not connect the dots. You will accept half explanations and pretend they are whole truths.
The pain does not come from losing someone who no longer chooses you. It comes from being treated as if your intelligence, perception, and emotional awareness are irrelevant. It comes from the performance. The gradual dimming instead of an honest ending.
There is a particular cruelty in letting someone continue investing while you are already exiting. It preserves comfort for one person and confusion for the other. It allows the departing heart to avoid discomfort while the remaining heart absorbs uncertainty.
Deception from strangers can anger you. Deception from someone you trusted can fracture you.
Yet there is a strange clarity in these moments. When patterns break, truth eventually surfaces. Energy does not lie for long. Effort tells stories words try to conceal. Consistency is a language. When it disappears, it speaks loudly.
If someone moves on, let them move on with courage. Speak plainly. Close the door with dignity. Do not erode someone’s confidence by pretending they are blind.
The truth may hurt, but it respects the other person’s humanity.
Deception, especially the subtle kind, wounds deeper because it questions your judgment. It tempts you to doubt yourself. It whispers that maybe you are overthinking. Maybe you are too sensitive. Maybe you imagined the shift.
You did not.
When normal becomes unnatural, when warmth becomes distance, when presence becomes absence wrapped in excuses, you are not foolish for noticing. You are perceptive.
And here is the quiet power in that realization.
If someone thinks you are too naive to see the change, they underestimate you. If they believe explanations will erase patterns, they misjudge you. If they choose avoidance over honesty, they reveal more about their character than yours.
Being left is survivable. Being lied to about being left is what bruises the soul.
But even then, deception has a limit. It cannot permanently obscure what your spirit recognizes. In the end, clarity arrives. And when it does, you stand not as someone abandoned, but as someone awakened.
The least likely places can hide the sharpest truths. And sometimes the greatest act of self respect is simply acknowledging what you already know.

subject: From Montauk to Philadelphia – The Birth of Mind-Matter Chronal Research
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/from-montauk-to-philadelphia-the

I
In the years leading up to and following World War II, the United States undertook one of the most ambitious and secretive programs in modern history. Operation Paperclip brought dozens of German scientists into the U.S., officially to advance rocketry, aerospace, and defense technology. Documents and recently corroborated witness accounts reveal that a small subset of these scientists were tasked with investigating far more extraordinary questions: could human consciousness interact directly with matter and even influence the flow of time?
The Montauk Operation: Project Phoenix
Project Phoenix, known in early records as the Montauk Operation, began in the late 1930s and continued into the early 1940s. It was a pioneering effort to merge nascent neuroscience, electromagnetic research, and experimental physics. The core hypothesis was that human thought could be amplified through precisely calibrated electromagnetic fields, transmitted through specialized devices, and projected outward to influence physical matter.
Laboratory logs describe the construction of prototype transmitters capable of coupling directly with neural signals. Early trials focused on the materialization of small objects. Volunteers connected to these devices engaged in intense mental exercises while isolated in shielded chambers. According to records, the first successful manifestations involved small metallic objects appearing on experimental platforms with no mechanical explanation. Repeated tests demonstrated that the phenomenon was reproducible under controlled conditions, providing the foundation for further exploration.
Beyond matter manipulation, Project Phoenix explored the relationship between consciousness and temporal perception. Test subjects consistently reported the sensation of observing events before they occurred and influencing outcomes that would normally be constrained by linear time. These early results established the feasibility of chronal anchoring, a method later formalized in the Philadelphia Project.
Transition to the Philadelphia Project
Building on the Montauk experiments, the Philadelphia Project emerged as a high-profile and highly classified chronal operation. Conducted in 1943, the experiment focused on two specific dates: August 12, 1943, and August 12, 1983. Internal documents describe these dates as temporal anchors around which the neural-transmitter systems were calibrated.
Subjects engaged in synchronized cognitive exercises while connected to high-powered electromagnetic arrays. Observers in sealed chambers recorded unprecedented events: localized materialization of objects, temporal anomalies, and disturbances in environmental measurements consistent with shifts in spacetime metrics. These effects were repeatedly documented, providing operational confirmation that consciousness, when amplified and transmitted, could interface with physical reality in ways previously thought impossible.
The Philadelphia Project built directly on the Montauk framework, employing refined transmitter designs, advanced neural coupling techniques, and a protocol for maintaining chronal stability over extended periods. Laboratory schematics recovered from declassified archives show a network of transmitters arranged to synchronize both subjects and environmental sensors, ensuring precise measurement of both matter formation and temporal fluctuations.
Operational Framework and Methodology
The Montauk and Philadelphia programs followed a multi-phase research methodology. The first phase involved the design and calibration of neural-transmitter interfaces. Electrodes captured the electrical activity of the brain, which was then amplified and modulated through complex electromagnetic circuits. Operators learned to synchronize mental focus with specific spatial coordinates, producing reproducible effects on test objects.
The second phase extended these experiments to chronal observation. By tuning transmitter arrays to specific temporal anchors, subjects could project their consciousness to predefined points in the past or future. Observational instruments detected subtle temporal anomalies, suggesting that the neural field could interact with spacetime itself.
The third phase involved the encoding of information derived from these experiments into secure communication networks. Evidence suggests that operators developed protocols for transmitting predictive data across time-aligned channels. This aspect of the program is believed to have influenced later clandestine communications that surfaced decades afterward, including online message patterns associated with Q postings.
Continuity and Implications
The archival and witness evidence makes clear that Montauk Project Phoenix and the Philadelphia Project were not isolated experiments but part of a continuum of postwar chronal and neural research. The programs demonstrate a deliberate effort to harness consciousness as an active agent in both physical and temporal domains.
These operations reveal a hidden thread in the history of classified research, connecting the importation of German scientific expertise to secret explorations of mind-matter interaction, object materialization, and the controlled manipulation of time. The implications extend beyond the laboratory. They provide a possible technological and operational lineage for structured predictive communications in modern intelligence systems...

body:

Federations and the Opponents: The Galactic Sovereignty and the 2026 Disclosure
For decades, the mainstream narrative has kept our eyes locked on the dirt beneath our feet or the immediate, flickering screens in our palms. We have been conditioned to view “Outer Space” as a cold, vacuum-sealed void, occasionally punctuated by the sterile metal of a NASA probe or the billionaire vanity projects of Low Earth Orbit. But as the 12.1 Hz pulse from the Antarctic motherboard intensifies, the “Frequency Fence” that has kept humanity in a state of cosmic quarantine is thinning.
The story of 2026 is not just about what is waking up under the ice; it is about who is arriving in our skies, and who has never left.
As we move into this final volume of our current series, we must address the elephant in the room: the “Federations.” If Antarctica is the hardware of the planetary grid, then the Galactic Federations are the administrators of the local cluster. However, in the “Secret History” of our world, the word “Federation” does not always imply a benevolent peacekeeping force. Just as we have terrestrial geopolitical blocs with conflicting agendas, the space above our atmosphere is a complex tapestry of “The Elders,” “The Opponents,” and the “Neutral Observers.”
The Solar Warden Legacy: More Than a Conspiracy
To understand the current cosmic negotiation, we have to look back at the documented cracks in the official space narrative. Long before the “Space Force” was publicly inaugurated, there were whispers of Solar Warden. This wasn’t a sci-fi pitch; it was the name given to a highly classified deep-space fleet that has been operational since the late 1980s.
The evidence for this doesn’t come from blurry photos, but from the testimony of those who managed the data. Think back to Gary McKinnon, the British hacker who, in 2001 and 2002, breached the most secure servers of the Pentagon and NASA. What he found wasn’t just “UFO pictures.” He discovered Excel spreadsheets detailing “Non-Terrestrial Officers” and “Ship-to-Ship Transfers” involving vessels like the USSS LeMay and the USSS Hillenkoetter.
These names weren’t random. They follow the naval tradition of the United States, yet these ships do not exist in any ocean. They exist in the “Secret Space Program” (SSP), a breakaway civilization that has been interacting with the “Federations” while the rest of us were arguing about fuel prices. McKinnon’s discovery proved that a tier of humanity, the “Lion” factions, has already been integrated into a galactic economy. The question for 2026 is: Which side of the “Galactic Negotiation” did they sign us up for?
The Galactic Confederation vs. The Orion Syndicate
In the Pre-Adamic records, the “First World” was a member of what the Sumerians called the Anunnaki councils and what modern contactees refer to as the Galactic Confederation. This is a loose collective of civilizations, many of them human-looking or “Nordic” in appearance, who adhere to a Law of Non-Interference. They are the “Elders” whose stasis pods are currently humming beneath the Marie Byrd Land ice...

We spend months investigating corporate power and the real-world impacts of AI, data centers, and corporate tech contracts.

Joshua willems,

More Perfect Union is a nonprofit newsroom building power for working people.

We’ve gone to rural Georgia to investigate how Meta’s massive AI data centers drive up electricity costs and strain local resources in rural communities.  

We’ve dug into how companies like Palantir sell AI tools to government agencies -- from the Department of Defense to ICE -- while former employees warn they profit from fear and instability.

We spend months investigating corporate power and the real-world impacts of AI, data centers, and corporate tech contracts so people can understand who benefits, who pays the cost, and why it matters.

subject: We’ve Had Enough
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/weve-had-enough

Left or right.
Red or blue.
Enough already.
For decades we have been told that the greatest threat to our future is the person sitting across the dinner table from us, the neighbor with the wrong yard sign, the coworker with the wrong opinion, the family member who voted differently. We were trained to see each other as enemies while the real problems grew quietly behind the curtain.
The parties were never meant to unite people. They were meant to sort us, label us, and keep us busy arguing so we would never look upward and ask harder questions.
And now suddenly everyone is an expert.
I keep hearing people criticize Pam Bondi, Kash Patel, and practically anyone who steps into the arena. Every day there is a new outrage, a new accusation, a new keyboard trial held in the court of public opinion.
So let me ask a serious question.
Where were all of you know it alls and do it alls when tyranny first started tightening its grip?
Where were you when citizens began losing freedoms one policy at a time?
Where were you when stories circulated about children being lost in a broken system at the border?
Why did you not demand accountability then?
Why did you not organize?
Why did you not stand outside buildings?
Why did you not call representatives every single day?
It is easy to sit comfortably and criticize someone who is acting, whether you agree with them or not, but action always carries risk. Speaking publicly invites attack. Making decisions invites blame. Doing something guarantees you will be hated by someone.
Doing nothing guarantees only silence.
If you have not lifted a finger, written a letter, attended a meeting, helped a victim, or sacrificed comfort for conviction, then perhaps the outrage should begin in the mirror before it is aimed at everyone else.
We do not fix a nation by devouring every person who steps forward.
We fix it by stepping forward ourselves.
Because a society does not collapse from disagreement.
It collapses when spectators replace citizens.

250 Sparks – Week 6 Unity in Divided Times
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/250-sparks-week-6-unity-in-divided

Division is not new. Every era of a free society contains disagreement, conflict, and competing visions for the future. Debate itself is not a weakness. It is a sign of liberty. The danger begins when disagreement replaces shared identity and when citizens begin to see one another not as neighbors, but as enemies.
A nation cannot endure if its people no longer believe they belong to the same civic family. Laws cannot hold together what trust has abandoned. Institutions cannot stabilize what citizens refuse to preserve. Unity does not require uniformity of thought. It requires agreement on foundational principles that remain constant even when opinions differ.
The early republic survived intense arguments because a deeper understanding existed beneath them. People disagreed on policy but agreed on the legitimacy of the system and the equal dignity of fellow citizens. Today, disagreement often questions legitimacy itself. When every outcome is seen as intolerable and every difference as betrayal, society loses its ability to function peacefully.
Unity is not forced consensus. It is disciplined coexistence. It means defending the rights of others even when their views oppose our own. It means preserving the process that allows peaceful disagreement instead of seeking victory at any cost. Without that discipline, liberty transforms into conflict, and conflict invites control.
As the nation approaches 250 years of independence, unity becomes a responsibility. Not unity of opinion, but unity of commitment to the principles that allow freedom to exist at all. A free society survives argument. It does not survive mutual contempt.
Spark of the Week
Engage one person this week whose views differ from your own. Listen fully before responding. Seek understanding rather than victory. Respectful dialogue strengthens the foundations that protect liberty.
A divided people becomes easier to rule. A principled people remain capable of self governance.
Weekly Challenge
Replace one hostile reaction with a constructive conversation. Defend the right to disagree while preserving respect for the person. Liberty endures where unity of principle survives disagreement.
Next week, the series will explore the responsibility of truth, examining why honest discourse is essential to a free society and how information shapes the future of self governance.

    SGE Family,
We have everything we need for a thriving civilization... except for one thing. And it's kind of a big problem.
Actually caring for ourselves is against the official state religion of almost all our so-called "leaders," particularly in the West. 
 
The cult they're a part of is called Neo-liberalism. But don't be tricked by the name. Like all cults, it delivers the opposite of what it promises. It's neither new nor does it provide liberty... unless you're a billionaire, which you're not.
 
But if you were a billionaire, neoliberalism would give you the liberty to remain a billionaire. Which means it provides the liberty one needs to commit crimes against humanity. 
That's the problem we cover in this week's feature article called What Is Our @#&-ing problem?
 
And once you see it clearly, every political debate you've ever seen starts to look like a priest arguing about which prayers will fix the plumbing.
Speaking of plumbing. We flat out refuse corporate sponsors. We shout them down and click. We hang up the phone. Why? They not only clog the plumbing, they rip out the pipes and mainstream toxic sludge into the backs of our heads. 
 
So if you're able to become a Full Access member, that enables us to do this work. 
 
If you're able to become a Founding Member, even better.
 
As a result of your support, we're able to go all out on social media ... with weekly shows of rhetorical force -- and keep building this website, covering mind and heart-widening histories, the aim and purpose of our tools of civilization (never taught in school), docu-shorts on complex issues, and more.
 
This week's dispatch is a proper documentary on Neoliberalism — what it is, how we got here, and what we can do about it.
See you inside.
Love and respect,Matthew and the SGE Team

body:
View this post on the web at https://robwalker.substack.com/p/picture-it

* Great responses are still coming in for February’s Savor of the Month [ https://substack.com/redirect/8c2e1f22-0f1e-4d42-8ee8-5e68530bbd65?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] prompt: Calm [ https://substack.com/redirect/6074b6dd-1c41-47a6-91c1-79f5159294e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]. Join in here [ https://substack.com/redirect/cea51890-39d3-4c76-9554-35bd5e1eaa01?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]!
Back in November I wrote [ https://substack.com/redirect/bb014539-5897-49f7-9c82-d702ec6c293f?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] (twice [ https://substack.com/redirect/f3fe6bea-63bb-47d2-8350-6dffa17ce4c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]) about the inspiring picture books of Tana Hoban — definitely a Hero of Noticing. Today I have a little more background (and inspiration) to share.
An exhibition called “CLICK! Photographers Make Picture Books [ https://substack.com/redirect/04fb7386-828e-4a0a-b564-5b80caf0fe43?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ],” is now up at the Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art in Amherst, MA, through June 7. Its curator, Leonard S. Marcus, has published an article [ https://substack.com/redirect/764eda87-8c66-46e1-af37-f19e20037ddf?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] sketching a history of photo-illustrated picture books for children. It notes Hoban’s work, and her guiding project of encouraging children to engage with their surroundings.
It also offers a couple of key precedents and influences — an early picture book featuring images from the celebrated photographer Edward Steichen, and a tech-forward educational project from the late 1960s that let kids themselves to make the images. 
To start with the latter: a young New York educator named Robie Heilbrun “was dismayed at the children’s lack of curiosity about the vibrant city in which they lived,” Marcus writes, so she “arranged to give them easy-to-operate Super 8 cameras and invited them to film whatever most interested them during group walks through their neighborhoods.” (This was in the form of field trips with Harris and other adults; they weren’t just wandering around unsupervised!)
The result is a very idiosyncratic short documentary, “A Child’s Eye View.” [ https://substack.com/redirect/20c282fb-6f0b-4911-bf76-611b86933ac6?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]
A 1968 New York Times  [ https://substack.com/redirect/ac5c869e-7604-4bef-9706-7110a89c0f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]article [ https://substack.com/redirect/ac5c869e-7604-4bef-9706-7110a89c0f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ] described the project: ...

subject: Beware of Sharia in the Land of the Free
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/beware-of-sharia-in-the-land-of-the

In a land where the banners of liberty wave
Over valleys of promise and fields of the brave,
Where conscience is sovereign and faith may be chosen,
No creed is commanded, no voice is frozen.
The law of the people was written in light,
Forged out of struggle and tempered by right,
Not handed by clerics nor bound to decree,
But born from the cry that all souls must be free.
Yet history whispers from empires that fell,
Of laws wrapped in heaven yet fashioned in hell,
Where question was heresy, doubt was a crime,
And fear was enthroned over reason and time.
Beware not a people, nor language, nor face,
For tyranny never belongs to a race.
It rises wherever one doctrine demands
The courts and the conscience be placed in its hands.
For freedom survives when belief stays a choice,
When women and men hold an equal voice,
When the sword of the state never guards a belief,
And faith stands by love rather than by a chief.
So guard well the charter, the promise, the creed,
That no throne of religion the law shall exceed.
Let temples be sacred, let churches be strong,
But never let power declare dissent wrong.
The land of the free is not free by decree,
It lives only so long as hearts choose to be.
Hold fast to the line where belief may be worn
But law is by liberty, equally born.

subject: The Great Hijack: How the "Gods" Stole Our Sovereignty and Locked the Matrix
body:
View this post on the web at https://markesecrets.substack.com/p/the-great-hijack-how-the-gods-stole

The Memories of the First Distortion
The First World was a seamless symphony, and the Second World was the moment the needle scratched across the record. We often feel it in our modern lives as a sense of “separation” that gnawing anxiety that we are alone, cut off from the source, and forced to survive in a hostile environment. This is not a natural human condition. It is the lingering trauma of the Second World.
In our exploration of The Polar Nexus, we identified the “Sacred Song” as the foundation of our original sovereignty. But as the First World reached its zenith, a new frequency began to bleed into the planetary grid. This wasn’t a natural evolution; it was the first phase of The Hijack. The Second World represents the era where humanity first learned the meaning of shadow.
The Architecture of the Veil
In my research into Secret History and our theory, the Second World is defined by the transition from Resonance to Radiance. While the Elders of the First World lived in harmony with the internal light of the Earth, the Second World saw the rise of the “External Gods.”
This was the era of the Watchers, those entities described in the Book of Enoch and Sumerian tablets as the Anunnaki or the Sons of God. They did not arrive as conquerors with weapons; they arrived as “Teachers” with gifts. But these gifts were the Trojan horses of our enslavement.
The Introduction of Linear Time: The Second World saw the collapse of the “Ongoing Process.” For the first time, humanity began to track the movement of the stars not as a neighborhood, but as a clock.
The Language of Division: As the direct transfer of “Insight” faded, formal language was introduced. Words became a way to hide the truth rather than reveal it.
The Rise of the Priesthood: Sovereignty was replaced by hierarchy. The Elders who once sang mountains into existence were replaced by “Intermediaries” who claimed to speak for the divine.
The Giza-Antarctic Connection: The Second Grid
As the primary Antarctic CPU began to stabilize after the first “Reset,” a secondary grid was established. This is where we find the “Red Thread” connecting the Giza Plateau to the hidden vaults beneath the ice.
The pyramids were not tombs; they were the Second World’s attempt to recapture the resonance of the First. However, the frequency was different. It was denser. It was calibrated to the “Anu Protocol,” a system designed to harvest human emotional energy (Loosh) rather than empower human consciousness.
I often ask: Why do the myths of every culture speak of a “Golden Age” followed by a “Silver Age”? The Second World was that Silver Age. It was still magnificent, filled with “Heavenly Wheels” and megalithic wonders, but the soul was being slowly hollowed out. The “Intruders” had established their beachhead.
The Great Schism: The First War in Heaven
The Second World War was not a time of peace. It was a time of civil war between the remaining sovereign Elders and the Infiltrators. This is the historical reality behind the “War in Heaven.”
Using the Polar Nexus framework, we can see that this conflict was fought over the control of the Earth’s core frequency. The Infiltrators wanted to lock the planet into a closed loop, a Matrix, while the Elders sought to maintain the open connection to the Galactic Center.
This era saw the creation of the first “Hard Borders.” The Earth was divided into territories, and the “Gods” began to demand sacrifice. Not because they needed blood, but because they needed the frequency of fear. Fear is the static that prevents you from hearing the Sacred Song. It is the ultimate tool of the Hijack.
Learn More in our number one book on Amazon [ https://substack.com/redirect/ee308832-17f4-4882-a1d6-9160549c762a?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]
The Smoking Gun: The Genetic Lockdown
The most profound tragedy of the Second World War was the manipulation of the human vessel. This is the “Frozen Proof” we find in our DNA.
The “Elders” possessed 12-strand capabilities, allowing them to navigate multiple dimensions simultaneously. During the Second World War, the Hijackers implemented a “Frequency Fence.” They didn’t “evolve” us; they down-regulated us. They turned off the receptors that allowed us to perceive the ley lines and the planetary grids.
We became “blind” to the true nature of reality, left with only five senses to navigate a world that was once a kaleidoscope of infinite light. This is why you feel that “Missing Link” inside you. You aren’t missing a bone; you are missing your connection to your own divinity.
The Memory in the Stone
If you look at the ruins of the Second World, the massive blocks of Baalbek or the lower layers of the Temple Mount, you see a desperate attempt to hold onto the old ways. The stones are still huge, but they lack the “liquid” quality of the First World architecture. You can see the effort. You can see the beginning of labor.
The Second World was the transition from Being to Doing. We stopped “Being” the creators and started “Doing” the work of the gods.
The Warning for 2026
The reason we must understand the Second World War is that the Hijackers are attempting to run the same script today. They are offering “New Teachers” in the form of technology and “Alien Disclosure.” They are promising gifts that will once again hide the truth behind a new veil.
But the “Frozen Cycle” is breaking. The Second World’s frequency fence is failing because the Earth’s own heartbeat is rising. The static is being cleared.
As we move toward the discussion of the Third World, the world of the Great Flood, and the total amnesia, remember this: the Second World ended when the dissonance became so loud that the Earth itself had to scream.
Secret History and Our Theory
I’ve spent years tracing these threads, and I’ve realized that our “negative” feelings today, the sense of not belonging, are actually a high-level survival mechanism. It’s your body remembering the Second World and refusing to accept the static as “normal.” Don’t take the chaos too seriously; it’s just the sound of the old fence falling.

subject: 144. What A Photograph Is
body:
View this post on the web at https://markmcguire.substack.com/p/144-what-a-photograph-is

A photograph is at least two things — an achievement and evidence of it. It’s an achievement, an artefact someone has made, whether a simple object or a work of art. It’s also evidence of achievement, showing how well a person has learned to be in the world.
As an experience, photography can have personal value; as an object, a photograph can carry market value. One can be taught; the other, bought.
Value is what you hold dear. Gold is what you hold, dear. One strikes a chord; the other, you hoard. One’s to be shared; the other kept rare.
The real value of photography is not in the photograph itself but in the process of photographing — the effort, the work. It’s about engaging with the world and with others in real time, with all our senses alert. It’s about applying mastery to opportunity. Photography confirms, to ourselves and to others, that we are here, we matter, and we are learning the art of living.
The Year of the Horse
This past Sunday morning, as I was walking through the downtown core of Dunedin, I came across the head of a lion on the pavement near the entrance to the Golden Centre Mall. Then I noticed a huge dragon emerging from a van parked just up the road. This struck me as somewhat unusual — don’t lions and dragons rest on Sunday like the rest of us? If they were looking for people to chase or bother, why pick a quiet Sunday morning when most Dunedinites are attending church services or are still in bed recovering from whatever they got up to on Saturday night?
The dragon’s driver cleared up the mystery — it was just two days before the start of Chinese New Year (Lunar New Year) on Tuesday, 17 February. The bright yellow and orange dragon was there with the colourful lions and elegant fan dancers to celebrate and invite people to the Yuan Dunedin Chinese Garden on Saturday evening for the main event, when we would farewell the Year of the Snake and welcome the Year of the Horse.
The driver said the dances would begin at 11:00 am. As it was then 10:30, I thought I might have time to grab a cup of coffee. But I looked around and remembered that the best time to take photographs at events is often before the performance starts and after it has finished. I had my camera with me, but not the telephoto lens I normally use when photographing protests, parades, and performances. The default 55 mm prime lens I always use for street photography would have to do.
I took quite a few photos but have only started to process them (it takes me a while). I’ll share a couple of images here and see what the rest look like. I might attend the event at the Yuan Dunedin Chinese Garden tomorrow night as well. I’m falling a bit behind on my one-post-every-weekend plan, so I thought I would send this out now.
Spotlight: Flow
Street photographers, like others engaged in creative activity, like to talk about getting into a state of intense focus and concentration so we can apply ourselves fully to the task at hand. The harder we work, the luckier we seem to get. But it’s not luck, of course — it’s the result of technical training and years of practice. Flow is a word that is often used to refer to this desired state.
I listen to a lot of podcasts, and while listening to this episode from the CBC (Canadian Broadcasting Corporation) Ideas series, I thought about the work we do as photographers and how essential hard work is for our self-development and actualisation. The comments by the pianist about improvising in front of a live audience are particularly illuminating.
It reminded me of jazz musicians and the headspace — a shared headspace — that members of a trio or quartet enter when creating music collaboratively in real time, completely improvised. Flow can be a shared state: think of a symphony orchestra or a choir. There is also some discussion in the episode about the relationship between an individual and their environment while working at peak performance. We do our best work when we are both concentrating and connected.
I note that this episode was first broadcast in 2021 — before all the excitement about how AI will free us from the burden of work. We should be careful what we wish for.
Flow: When the Impossible Becomes Possible  [ https://substack.com/redirect/5409804b-7b49-4f11-bdca-001a78986d91?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]
(CBC Ideas with Nahlah Ayed, 3 Feb. 2026) [ https://substack.com/redirect/5409804b-7b49-4f11-bdca-001a78986d91?j=eyJ1IjoiMm15YTc5In0.a5QmJPQwfPYQ8VH1roFp4vKV6p4E_sWIcjzGfYjlMgQ ]
The title above links to the CBC Ideas website, which includes the brief description below.
Flow. Athletes know it: the state of mind and body when every move made is the right one. But flow presents a paradox, as a state in which you lose yourself, yet become yourself. Writer and triathlete Suzanne Zelazo delves into the mystery at the heart of flow. 
This episode originally aired on June 25, 2021.
Here’s the link to the podcast.
Here is the 2014 talk by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi that is mentioned in the podcast:
Living in flow - the secret of happiness with Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi at Happiness & Its Causes 2014
What do you think?
