subject: Urgent Question Are Earth’s Magnetic Poles Really Shifting And Why Aren’t We Being Told
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/urgent-question-are-earths-magnetic

Across social media amateur observations and even some pilots and sailors people are reporting strange things compasses behaving oddly navigation apps needing recalibration and claims that the sun appears to rise or set in unfamiliar positions. Some are estimating the magnetic field is off by as much as 90 degrees.
That sounds catastrophic.
So naturally the question follows
If something this big is happening why are governments and the media not sounding the alarm
What We Actually Know About Earth’s Magnetic Pole
Earth’s magnetic pole is not fixed.
It has always moved.
Scientists from the NOAA and USGS track it constantly because airplanes ships missiles satellites and even smartphone maps depend on it.
Here is the verified reality
The magnetic north pole has been drifting for centuries
Since the 1990s it accelerated dramatically
It moved from Canada toward Siberia at unusually fast speed
Because of this the World Magnetic Model had to be updated early in 2019
Navigation systems worldwide were recalibrated
So yes something unusual is happening
But not a 90 degree flip overnight
Why Your Compass May Seem Wrong
Magnetic north is not true north
Your compass points to the magnetic field lines not the planet’s axis. The difference between them is called declination and it varies by location.
As the pole drifts faster
Old maps become inaccurate
Survey markers go off alignment
Phone compasses need recalibration
Sun position appears slightly shifted relative to landmarks
Humans are very sensitive to familiar patterns. A change of only a few degrees can feel dramatic
The Sun Rising in the Wrong Place
The sun itself is not moving relative to Earth’s rotation
But what can change
Atmospheric refraction
Observer reference points
Magnetic versus geographic alignment
Seasonal solar path perception
GPS correction adjustments
People who use buildings trees or streets as sunrise markers may perceive major displacement when it is actually only a few degrees which is significant for navigation but not civilization ending
Why No Emergency Announcement
Because to scientists this is serious but not sudden
The agencies studying Earth’s magnetic field including NASA view it as part of a long geophysical process called geomagnetic excursion or reversal behavior
Magnetic pole shifts occur over decades to centuries not days
Governments typically issue public alerts only when an immediate safety risk exists infrastructure will fail imminently or public action is required
Right now the effects mainly impact aviation charts military navigation geological surveys and satellite calibration not daily survival
Why It Feels Hidden
There is a perception gap
Scientists discuss this in technical publications navigation bulletins and aviation updates not prime time news broadcasts. The public encounters the effects first and assumes silence equals secrecy
But the data is published the updates are issued and the audience is specialized
The average citizen rarely reads geomagnetic model revisions
Last Words
The poles have not suddenly rotated 90 degrees
They are moving unusually fast
Compasses are being affected
Navigation systems worldwide are adjusting
What is unfolding is not an overnight disaster but a long planetary process. The concern is not that the world is ending but that Earth’s magnetic shield may be entering a new phase one that scientists quietly monitor while infrastructure is slowly adapted around it.

subject: President Trump Will Fulfill Prophecy: God’s David for a New Era
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/president-trump-will-fulfill-prophecy

Across the pages of history, God has raised leaders in times of great turmoil to guide His people toward purpose, justice, and divine promise. In our current era, many believers see President Donald Trump as one such figure, a modern-day David, called by God to prepare the nation for a golden age. This is not mere political commentary; it is a spiritual perspective rooted in faith and observation.
Throughout Scripture, David was chosen not for his worldly power but for his heart, his courage, and his devotion to God. Similarly, President Trump’s rise and influence are being interpreted by many as more than political happenstance. He embodies the decisive, fearless leadership necessary to steer a nation through moral, economic, and cultural turbulence.
This prophetic view holds that God has a plan: a season in which His people will prosper materially, spiritually, and communally, a time to serve, to worship, and to grow closer to Him. Under this divine framework, leadership is not only about policy but about enabling the conditions for righteousness and devotion to flourish. President Trump’s role, in this lens, is to safeguard these conditions, preparing the nation for the fulfillment of biblical prophecy, including the eventual events of the Book of Revelation.
Critics may scoff, calling it political idolization or exaggeration, but history shows that God often works through unexpected vessels. David was a shepherd, a warrior, and a poet before he became king. Leaders anointed by God do not always fit the conventional mold; they are instruments of divine purpose. President Trump’s achievements, but resilience, and influence, despite relentless opposition, are seen by many as proof of God’s hand at work.
We are called not only to observe but to participate. As a nation and as a community of believers, the opportunity exists to align with this divine purpose, to prepare our hearts, our communities, and our nation for a season of spiritual and practical prosperity. This is a moment to embrace hope, courage, and steadfast faith, knowing that God’s plan unfolds even when human understanding is limited.
President Trump’s role, in this prophetic vision, is a reminder that God’s sovereignty is real, that His plans are perfect, and that even in turbulent times, there is a path to blessing and preparation. The golden age is not a distant dream, it is a calling for action, faith, and alignment with the divine purpose.

subject: He Was My Father. He Deserved Honors
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/he-was-my-father-he-deserved-honors

I was raised in a Democratic home.
My father was a staunch Democrat and a Vietnam veteran. To him, party loyalty wasn’t political strategy, it was identity. It was discipline. It was almost military.
“It doesn’t matter if your candidate sucks,” he would say. “You stick to the party, son.”
My grandfather, however, was conservative. And somewhere between the kitchen table arguments and front porch debates, I heard both sides.
One day my dad looked at me and said, “You were raised to be a Democrat.”
Wait.
What?
Then he’d talk about how his father raised him conservative.
And that’s when that famous line would echo in my mind:
Do as I say, not as I do.
If ever an oxymoron existed… geez.
When I enlisted, I did so as a Democrat. The military has a way of refining you. It strips things down to principle. Oath. Constitution. Duty.
By the time I exited service, my mindset had shifted.
I had already had enough of George H. W. Bush. I stood at parade rest for hours in the freezing cold at his inauguration. His first stop was right in front of me. I saluted until he moved out of sight. Something about the tone, the policies, and especially that “New World Order” language never sat right in my gut.
Then came Bill Clinton pushing the Brady Bill.
Hold up.
“Shall not be infringed” was not a slogan to me. It wasn’t a bumper sticker. It had been instilled in me since first grade. Words meant things. The Constitution meant something.
So when my dad and I went to the polls that year, it felt routine.
We walked in.
We voted.
We walked out.
We got in the truck.
Just as we pulled into the driveway he asked, “Who did you vote for?”
“I thought—”
He cut me off. “Did I tell you to think?”
“I voted for Ross Perot.”
Two hours.
Two hours of lecture.
Years later Barack Obama was in the White House. My dad voted for him. I did not. We debated birth certificates, policies, direction of the country. He wasn’t convinced at first, but something had shifted in him. You could hear it in his voice.
Then 2016 came.
We had a system. Every two weeks, like clockwork, we’d call and catch up.
He called.
“Who did you vote for?”
“Dad, you don’t need to ask me. You already know. I didn’t vote for the Manchurian to begin with. You did.”
Silence.
I waited.
“You didn’t do that again, did you?”
Silence.
Then finally:
“Hell no I didn’t. I voted for Trump.”
I danced a jig in a public parking lot.
I told him I was proud of him.
From that moment on, every time Donald Trump spoke, my dad took notes. Literal notes. He intended to hold him accountable to every promise. Every two weeks he sounded more convinced, more engaged, more hopeful. You would never have guessed a lifelong Democrat had existed.
On May 25, 2017, Agent Orange took the last thing it could take.
His life.
I called the funeral home, a multi-generational operation. The grandson was running it now. We grew up together.
“I need to make his military arrangements.”
There was a pause.
“You might want to sit down.”
He explained that in 2011 burial benefits had been reduced. Most of the honors were gone. Basically, Dad would receive a flag folding team.
That wasn’t going to cut it. They didn’t tell him  
Not for a man who served his country.
Not for a man who carried the cost of Vietnam in his bloodstream until the end.
I emailed representatives. Congressmen. Offices that return polished responses and accomplish nothing.
It was as useless as an elevator in an outhouse.
Then I saw the news criticizing POTUS for using Twitter.
The lights came on.
If that’s where he speaks, that’s where I’ll go.
The next day my son was coming to ride home with me. If I was going to do this, it had to be now.
I set up a YouTube livestream titled, DIY How to Shave My Testicles.  to get attention. Waist up only. Soaped head to toe. Fifty guys in the chat wondering when did the show start and me second guessing this. 
I apologized for the clickbait.
Then I told the story.
I gave it until midnight for traction. There was attention, just  not the kind I wanted.
So I made a decision.
I took that very video, and I uploaded it.
I uploaded it to the President on Twitter.
Heart pounding harder than any drumroll.
I waited until 2 a.m., fully expecting black helicopters to show. 
Nothing.
Morning came. I turned on the TV. The President was speaking at the Air Force Academy graduation. I was getting discouraged. 
Then my phone rang.
A tone I only heard when the number wasn’t in my contacts.
Oh no. 
I answered to attempt to sound like a woman  
A woman asked for my full name. I tried to disguise my voice. She laughed. I laughed. I asked how much trouble I was in.
“None,” she said.
She explained her title and that she was calling from the White House.
Then she said something I’ll never forget.
“The President does not think he will have time to change this in time for your father. But he wants you to know that it will never happen again.”
The drive back home to my roots was long and heavy.
We arrived after visiting hours. I wanted time alone.
We rang the bell. My friend opened the door. He looked excited.
“Who do you know?” he asked.
“What?”
“Come with me.”
He opened the chapel doors.
There sat my father in a flag draped casket.
And beside him stood an Airman so he wouldn’t be alone.
That was the moment the emotional wall cracked. The wall our fathers told us that men don’t let crack.
My dad received full military honors.
A man who never knew my name had made sure respect was shown. Not because of me. Not because of a video.
But because having honor and honoring those who served matters.
Because when we see a veteran, we stand.
When the Anthem plays, we stand.
When a flag is folded, we stand.
My sword and shield will hold the line until one of us falls Mr. President. 
Always faithful.
Dad, I held on till the end.
I hope it didn’t embarrass you.
President Trump sir, Dad, I salute you. 🫡

subject:
More Perfect Union is the fastest growing progressive political
 channel on YouTube
body:
More Perfect Union is an Emmy-winning, nonprofit newsroom and the fastest growing progressive political channel on YouTube.

Hi Joshua willems, it’s Faiz from More Perfect Union. We were recently featured in the Washington Post about how we’re developing the fastest-growing online political content on the left -- breaking through partisanship to reach working people and disaffected Trump voters.

When we founded More Perfect Union, we hoped to create something that could counter the agenda-setting power Fox News has on the right. Instead of focusing solely on the latest outrage from Republicans, we wanted to proactively center the needs of working people with documentary-style videos that truly tell their stories.

It’s gratifying to see our approach catching on. As the Washington Post notes, More Perfect Union has added more YouTube subscribers than any other progressive political channel in the last 90 days.

We’ve achieved a lot in the last 5 years. We’re nowhere close to achieving everything we set out to do -- but we’ve developed an approach that’s working, and it’s time to keep expanding it.

That’s why we’re expanding our content, to develop voices in sports, music, food, and other parts of culture. Corporate greed is everywhere, so we need to be too.

We’re also launching a campus program to train students in our model of advocacy journalism. Elise Joshi, the head of More Perfect Union’s campus program told the Post: “My generation as a whole are fed up with a world built by and for billionaires.”

More Perfect Union will give them the tools to fight back.

None of this work is cheap. But all of it is necessary.

As we work to bring our investigative journalism to a wider audience online and expand our work onto college campuses, we need your support. Power our viral video reports and help us reach more working people across the country by making a donation to More Perfect Union today.

250 Sparks – Week 5 The Cost of Complacency and the Duty of Vigilance
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/250-sparks-week-5-the-cost-of-complacency

Freedom rarely disappears in a dramatic moment. More often, it fades through comfort, routine, and the quiet belief that someone else will guard it. Complacency is not loud. It does not announce surrender. It feels like stability. It feels like normalcy. Yet history shows that liberty weakens most when people assume it no longer requires their attention.
The endurance of a free society depends on awareness. Laws may be written. Institutions may stand. Rights may be declared. None of them sustain themselves. They require citizens who observe, question, and remain present. When people disengage, authority naturally expands into the space left behind. Not always through force, often simply through absence of resistance.
Complacency begins in small habits. Choosing not to learn because it feels complicated. Choosing silence because speaking feels inconvenient. Choosing comfort over responsibility because daily life already feels demanding. Individually these decisions seem harmless. Collectively they reshape a culture. A population that stops noticing eventually stops deciding.
Vigilance does not mean constant outrage. It does not require perpetual conflict. It means awareness. Understanding how decisions are made. Paying attention to what changes and why. Teaching the next generation that freedom is not inherited intact, but maintained through participation. Vigilance is steady. It is deliberate. It is disciplined.
As America approaches 250 years of independence, the lesson remains unchanged from the founding era. Liberty survives where citizens remain awake to it. It weakens where comfort replaces responsibility.
Spark of the Week
Choose one area of civic life that has been taken for granted. Learn how it functions. Understand who influences it. Observe how decisions are made. Awareness is the first defense against erosion.
Complacency weakens a nation quietly. Vigilance strengthens it just as quietly. The difference is attention.
Weekly Challenge
Replace one passive habit with an informed one. Observe instead of assuming. Ask instead of dismissing. Remain present even when nothing feels urgent. Liberty endures where vigilance lives.
Next week, we turn to unity in divided times, exploring how shared principles can hold a nation together when tension rises and opinions clash. A free society cannot survive prolonged fragmentation. It must rediscover the foundations that bind it together.

subject: 💔 My relationship humiliation made me hide...
body:
So I kept it to myself and just suffered through. If that's you right now...
 
 

Hi Joshua,

 

I can remember the night I felt the most alone I have ever felt in my life. I was sitting in my apartment by myself.

 

My first wife had just yelled at me and slammed down the phone. The silence after the spike was raw and visceral. I started crying.

 

We'd already been separated for months, she took our son when she moved out, and I was daily feeling alone.

 

But that night the loneliness hit deeper than ever before. It felt complete, severe and impossible to overcome.

 

And then my dad called seconds later and made it much worse.

 

It wasn't his fault. I saw his name pop up on my phone.

 

I immediately felt this surge of hope rush through my body... somebody cared about me... somebody was reaching out.

 

But that excitement was immediately followed by this terrible, deep, unstoppable sense of loneliness and depression.

 

Here's the thing: my family didn't know what was going on. I hadn't shared our separation with anybody. Zero family or friends knew. 

 

My thoughts at the time... I can't tell my dad what's going on. I have to fix this relationship issue on my own. 

 

I felt trapped. I felt like I had to keep it private & stand strong.

 

As far as anyone else knew, we were living three hours away in a different city for work. As far as my family knew, everything was fine in our marriage.

 

The humiliation was so heavy. I felt like such a failure. The pain ran deep. I was carrying this burden completely alone.

 

I lied that night and told my dad everything was great. 

 

What a bittersweet moment... happy someone cared about me, happy my dad was randomly calling just to check in. But I also knew when I picked up the phone, I couldn't be honest with him. I couldn't tell him what was really going on.

 

And that just amplified the loneliness I felt.

 

If this resonates with you... if today feels lonely even though maybe you're not technically alone... I want you to know I've been there.

 

Maybe you're single and Valentine's Day is just highlighting this.

 

Maybe you're with someone but you feel completely unseen.

 

Maybe you bought the flowers or made the reservation or did all the "right things" today, but underneath it all there's this feeling that something fundamental isn't connecting.

 

Maybe you're the only one in your relationship willing to look at the hard stuff. That's a brutal kind of loneliness. It sucks to feel like, "I'm alone and I can't let anyone in."

 

Here's what I learned after that difficult life season: starting relationship work alone is an act of courage.

 

When I finally started understanding my own relationship patterns... my personality type, my cognitive functions, my way of processing the world... that's when things began to shift.

 

Not because my ex-wife suddenly changed, but because I could finally see what was actually happening between us. 

 

My first marriage ultimately ended and shortly after I met and fell in love with Antonia. And 16 years later, we are deeply in love as pair bond partners.

 

One of the things that helped us get there... to build something different... was understanding our personality maps.

 

Having a shared language for our cognitive functions and type dynamics means we can actually resolve conflict instead of just repeating it.

 

Based on the personality maps we actually use as a couple, we personally wrote and recorded an entire program for you: Couples Mapping 

Couples Mapping teaches you how to create your relationship map.

 

And if you are alone in your desire to grow, the Couples Mapping program can be done solo. In fact, that's how a lot of people start.

 

First, you learn your map. Next, you learn your partner's map. The, you begin to see where the wires are crossing, where you're speaking different languages, where you're accidentally hurting each other.

 

Eventually, if they're ready, your partner may join you in this work. But that's not required for your relationship to benefit.

 

Understanding your personality maps changes things, even if it's one-sided at first.

I know what it's like to be the only one willing to look at the hard truth. Feeling like you're trying and they're not. Wondering if you're crazy for still hoping things could be different.

 

I don't think you're crazy. I think you care.

 

Relationship work alone is an act of courage.

Much Love,

Joel Mark Witt & Antonia Dodge

subject: Point of Order
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/point-of-order

Weeks ago the major television networks and national outlets spoke with one voice. The Minnesota case dominated coverage, and the public was fed short clips and carefully selected phrases that carried a clear implication. Viewers were meant to feel as though the country was being invaded, that chaos was swelling, and that only one political interpretation made sense of it all. The repetition was relentless. Experts were lined up. Panels nodded in agreement. Social feeds amplified the same angles.
Then the shootings happened. Within minutes, headlines hardened into conclusions. The framing was immediate and decisive. Before investigations matured, before all facts were known, the narrative was already written. It did not evolve from evidence. It preceded it. Seconds of footage were treated as certainty. Early speculation was treated as settled truth.
We have seen this pattern before. An event erupts. The public waits for clarity. Instead, clarity is replaced with storyline. Once the storyline is fixed, every development is filtered through it. Anything that reinforces it is highlighted. Anything that complicates it is buried.
Prior to Minnesota, the press corps seemed united in another certainty. They were convinced that Donald Trump would appear prominently in the Epstein documents. The phrase accountability echoed across every network. Commentators spoke as if the conclusion were inevitable. Night after night, viewers were primed for exposure.
Then the documents did not deliver the anticipated result. Trump was not in the files in the way many had forecast. Instead, other prominent names emerged, including individuals connected to circles friendly to the very outlets demanding accountability.
And just like that, the drumbeat stopped.
Accountability, once the moral rallying cry, faded into a whisper. Panels moved on. Headlines shifted. The urgency evaporated. The same voices that insisted transparency was non negotiable grew cautious and quiet when the transparency cut closer to home.
This is the point of order.
If accountability is a principle, it cannot be conditional. If truth matters, it must matter even when it disrupts preferred outcomes. If journalists claim to hold power accountable, they must apply that standard evenly, not selectively.
The public notices the asymmetry. They see how quickly stories are amplified when they wound one side, and how swiftly they cool when they implicate allies. They see how language shifts. How outrage is rationed. How silence can be as strategic as noise.
Media institutions hold enormous influence. They shape perception before facts are fully known. They define villains and heroes in real time. With that power comes responsibility. Not to narrative. Not to ideology. But to evidence.
When coverage begins with a conclusion and hunts for support, journalism becomes theater. When accountability is demanded only for opponents, credibility erodes.
The issue is not whether any one figure is guilty or innocent. The issue is whether the standard is consistent.
Point of order. Apply the same measure to everyone. Or admit that the measure was never the point at all.

subject: The Symphony of the First Dawn
body:
View this post on the web at https://markesecrets.substack.com/p/the-symphony-of-the-first-dawn

The Memory of a Sun That Never Set
There is a specific vibration that resides within the human heart. a resonance that feels like a forgotten language. It is the memory of the First World. Before the Great Reset, before the “Frozen Cycle” locked our planet in a grip of amnesia, and long before the current Matrix was calibrated, there was an era of such profound harmony that modern language can barely describe it. This was the time of the First World, a period where humanity lived not as subjects, but as sovereign architects of reality.
In my work with Secret History and our theory, I have often spoken of the “Red Thread,” that single line of truth that connects our fractured past. Today, we follow that thread back to its very beginning. We are not looking for fossils or primitive tools; we are looking for the “Sacred Song,” the fundamental frequency upon which the First World was built.
A World Built on Light and Sound
The First World was not a place of labor as we understand it today. It was a realm of Resonance. To the inhabitants of this era, the physical world was not a solid, stubborn obstacle to be overcome with muscle and steel. Instead, they perceived the environment as a fluid symphony of vibrations.
Imagine a landscape where the mountains themselves felt “alive” and responsive to human consciousness. This was the era of the Pre-Adamic Kings, the sovereign rulers who reigned before the current Matrix system was fully calibrated and locked. These beings were the conductors of the planetary frequency. When they desired to raise a structure, what we now find as the impossible megalithic foundations of the world, they did not “build” them. They sang them into existence.
The architecture of the First World was frozen music. The great crystalline cities of Shambhalla and the pre-glacial hubs of Antarctica were constructed by harmonizing with the atomic structure of the stone itself. This is why the oldest ruins on Earth show no tool marks; they were formed by resonance, shaped by the will of a consciousness that understood its own divinity. In this world, there was no hunger, for the air itself was saturated with the energy of the “Sacred Song,” nourishing the body directly through the breath.
The Sovereignty of the Elders
The people of the First World, often referred to in my research as the Elders or the Pre-Adamic race, possessed a biology that was fundamentally different from ours. They were not yet degraded by the “Anu Protocol,” the frequency lock that limits our current lifespan and cognitive potential. They lived for what we would call millennia, but for them, time was not a linear march toward death; it was an “ongoing process” of expansion...

subject: The Architecture of Control
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-architecture-of-control

The Leverage Question
Every powerful institution insists it operates under rules. History shows rules matter most when they are tested.
For decades the public debate around intelligence agencies has focused on surveillance for security purposes. Terrorism espionage cyber warfare. The official mission has always been protection.
But among oversight lawyers retired investigators and technical auditors another concern has quietly persisted. Not foreign spying. Not counterterrorism.
Leverage.
The fear is not that information is collected. It is what happens when the information becomes useful against the people who govern.
How Compromise Actually Works
Blackmail rarely looks like a movie.
There is no smoky room and no dramatic confrontation. Instead the process is bureaucratic and patient. Analysts sometimes describe the concept as vulnerability mapping. A person with authority produces digital exhaust across thousands of systems. Travel records financial patterns private communications undisclosed relationships contradictions between public and private behavior.
A profile emerges.
In intelligence culture information has tiers of value. Most data is irrelevant. Some predicts behavior. A small fraction can redirect decisions.
Control does not require proving wrongdoing in court. It only requires convincing the subject exposure is possible.
The Quiet Pressure Mechanism
Several former compliance reviewers describe a scenario that worries watchdog officials more than overt corruption.
First information is discovered during a legitimate national security search. Second the information is stored rather than reported as unrelated. Third the subject becomes aware the information exists.
Nothing explicit needs to be said.
A postponed investigation a stalled confirmation a sudden leak rumor appearing in media or a private warning delivered indirectly can alter behavior faster than any law. Power responds to risk.
In that environment a secret becomes a steering wheel.
The More Dangerous Allegation
Some experts fear an even darker possibility. Not discovering compromising material but manufacturing it.
Digital systems allow evidence to exist before a person knows it exists. Metadata timestamps routing paths and account associations can be recorded in ways a nontechnical person cannot easily challenge. Even the suggestion that damaging material was found and documented can be enough.
The threat does not need to survive a trial. It only needs to survive a conversation.
A senior oversight staffer once summarized the concern bluntly. A person does not have to be guilty to become controllable. They only have to believe a system can make them appear guilty.
Why This Would Matter
Government depends on independent decision making. Legislators judges and executives must believe they can act without hidden coercion.
If individuals fear unseen dossiers exist on everyone then authority shifts away from elected leadership toward whoever controls the archive.
The danger is not ideological. It does not belong to a party. Any group holding undisclosed leverage over multiple officials would effectively hold influence over policy itself.
That possibility has haunted democratic systems since long before computers. Digital storage simply makes the archive permanent.
After the disclosures of Edward Snowden the public learned how broadly information could be collected. The unresolved question was never just privacy. It was internal misuse.
Why Proof Is So Rare
Blackmail systems are uniquely resistant to exposure.
Targets rarely report pressure because reporting confirms vulnerability. Agencies deny misuse because classified material cannot be publicly debated. Courts struggle because evidence cannot easily be introduced without revealing sources.
The result is a permanent stalemate. Allegations circulate while documentation remains sealed.
Most accusations collapse from lack of proof. Yet the structure that would enable them undeniably exists.
The Real Issue
The core issue is not whether a hidden network currently controls government. There is no verified public evidence proving such a coordinated program.
The issue is capability combined with secrecy.
If a system can collect everything and store it indefinitely and access is limited to a small internal circle then theoretical leverage becomes structurally possible. Democratic trust depends on confidence that possibility is never used.
Citizens cannot audit classified databases. They rely on oversight and law.
Trust therefore rests on people not systems.
Factional Politics and the Activation Question
Another recurring allegation within whistleblower circles involves internal political factionalism during presidential cycles. Specifically, some former staffers and contractors have claimed that elements inside federal bureaucracies favored certain establishment figures during primary contests and quietly worked to disadvantage outsiders.
Two names frequently cited in political reporting during the 2012 and 2016 eras are Paul Ryan [ chatgpt://generic-entity?number=0 ] and Mitt Romney [ chatgpt://generic-entity?number=1 ]. Both were viewed at different times as standard bearers of traditional Republican leadership. Romney secured the party’s nomination in 2012. Ryan later rose to Speaker of the House and was widely discussed in earlier cycles as a potential future presidential contender.
The allegation is not that ballots were altered or that explicit illegal directives were issued. Rather, the claim centers on a subtler mechanism: that institutional actors who preferred predictable candidates may have leveraged informal networks, media relationships, opposition research pipelines, and strategic leaks to create favorable or unfavorable conditions.
Political professionals understand that campaigns are rarely decided by speeches alone. They are shaped by timing, narrative framing, and the flow of damaging or protective information. If individuals inside powerful institutions held undisclosed material on multiple candidates, the selective release or suppression of such information could shift momentum without leaving fingerprints.
There is no verified public evidence demonstrating a coordinated intelligence effort to promote or undermine specific presidential hopefuls. However, the perception that entrenched actors may attempt to steer outcomes is fueled by observable patterns in modern politics:
• rapid dissemination of damaging stories during primary surges
• selective investigative intensity
• sudden shifts in elite endorsements
• media narratives aligning with institutional preferences
In highly competitive primaries, even minor information asymmetries can alter trajectories. A campaign does not need to be destroyed outright. It only needs to be slowed long enough for another to consolidate support.
The deeper concern raised by critics is structural rather than personal. If bad actors inside a system believed a particular candidate represented a threat to institutional continuity, could they justify informal coordination to protect what they view as stability?
That question has surfaced repeatedly in modern politics, across parties and administrations.
Again, there is no conclusive proof that intelligence resources were deployed to advance or hinder the presidential ambitions of Ryan, Romney, or any other figure. But the suspicion persists because modern political ecosystems blur the boundaries between government, party leadership, media influence, and private sector data operations.
When institutions become intertwined, distinguishing routine political maneuvering from improper coordination becomes extraordinarily difficult.
And in that ambiguity, distrust grows.

subject: 👉 How to stop hating Valentines Day...
body:
It took some shadow work, and learning to get over myself.
 
 

Hi Joshua,

 

I don't know if you're like me, but I used to hate Valentine's Day.

 

I would look at this holiday every year and I'd feel like it was a commercialized, forced experience that was inauthentic. In my mind it was fake and silly and plastic and gross. Blah.

 

But I'll tell you, at the age I'm at now, after doing a lot of work with my personality type, my heart has softened and I see it differently.

 

Holidays are cultural touchpoints. These are recurring moments every year where we're invited to pause and focus on something important, together as a culture.

 

With ENFP preferences, that wasn't always obvious to me. Memory (Introverted Sensing) is not my strength. But over time, I've learned to appreciate that recurring holiday moments are important.

 

As I've been working on my shadow functions, I've also realized that there's an external relationship energy that Harmony (Extraverted Feeling) tunes into. I often miss this as an ENFP.

 

As I've tuned into why we celebrate cultural moments I've stopped hating Valentine's Day.

 

In fact, I've actually learned to appreciate it for what it is.

 

Of course, I would never set up a system like this, but I like that people thought to give our culture a recurring situation to think about love.

 

The truth is we live in a culture that expresses itself through purchased gifts and flowers and cards. Trying to change that is like attempting to boil the ocean.

 

And, I've realized this doesn't necessarily make it wrong or bad. This is the one thing I've had to contend with. The commercial aspect doesn't necessarily ruin the intent behind the gesture or offering.

 

And as I tune into the intent behind Valentine's Day, I find the intent is good.

 

Valentine's Day is a cultural way to celebrate love, celebrate the person that's special to you, and celebrate your pair bond relationship together. 

 

This can be a magical, important moment for couples.

 

Here's what I know about my relationship with Antonia... I sometimes forget how blessed I am to have found the love of my life in my early 30s.

 

Yes, I had heartbreak and struggle in previous relationships, but I swear I hit the jackpot with Antonia.

 

And I've realized in recent years that not everyone is living inside the relationship they wish for. But I think most couples can have a powerful relationship if they have our secret weapon.

 

Our secret weapon as a couple is our personality maps and shared type language.

 

We have shared language and understanding of our functions and type dynamics. We use type to understand each other, not to win arguments.

 

Of course we still have conflict, type doesn't solve that. 

 

But it's better conflict that actually ends in resolution with faster cycle times.

 

So that brings us back to this holiday moment...

 

Tomorrow is Valentine's Day.

 

You might be buying flowers or making dinner reservations or doing the traditional things. And I think it's okay to tune in and join a cultural moment. 

 

I also get it if you're an iconoclast about it like I was. I ratify that too.

 

And if you're reading this and thinking about your relationship, if you're wondering whether there's something more underneath the surface that needs attention, maybe this weekend is also a good time to invest in understanding the source code running you and your partner.

 

We are offering our Couples Mapping program at 50% off this weekend. Use Code: VDAY26

 

Couples Mapping is probably our best home-study course.

 

In the course, Antonia and I personally teach the mapping process and show you how to see the patterns and challenges.

 

Even if you're the only one in your partnership ready to do this work right now, that's okay.

 

It starts with you understanding yourself and your partner better. The shared language comes later, but the understanding starts with one person willing to look.
Map Your Relationship Dynamics ⮕

Use Code: VDAY26
 


Much Love,

Joel Mark Witt & Antonia Dodge
Co-Founders | Personality Hacker

                  US non-farm payroll report tops expectations:
Non-farm payrolls increased by 130,000 and the unemployment rate
dropped to 4.3% in the US in January, signaling the US economy is
in a slightly stronger position than recent estimates. The report
from the Bureau of Labor Statistics beat a Dow Jones consensus
prediction of 55,000 new jobs, easing some concerns over a
slowing labor market. Crypto prices declined following the report
as analysts priced in the possibility of less aggressive rate
cuts in 2026.       BlackRock to put tokenized treasury fund on
Uniswap: BlackRock announced Wednesday it will put US tokenized
treasuries fund BUIDL on Uniswap in the financial giant’s first
major foray into decentralized finance. Tokenization company
Securitize will lead compliance and handle regulatory matters as
part of the deal.       Crypto and banking lobby still at an
impasse on CLARITY Act: The two sides reportedly were unable to
reach a compromise at a White House meeting this week after
banking industry participants presented a list of rules
restricting any stablecoin yield opportunities that went beyond
the current version of the CLARITY Act. Banks have drawn a hard
line around prohibiting stablecoin rewards for fear customers
will pull their money en masse.       BitMine Immersion buys more
Ethereum: BitMine Immersion Technologies announced this week it
acquired 40,613 ETH last week amid the crypto market pullback,
bringing the Ethereum treasury company’s total crypto stack to
approximately $9 billion at current market prices. The company

subject: [PODCAST #627] 👉 Sensing & Intuition Misreads: Stop Second-Guessing Your Type
body:
If you are second guessing your type it might be the way the functions are described.
 
 

Hi Joshua,

 

Antonia and I are shaping the podcast for the coming season and we’d love your input & advice. We created a quick 2-minute check-in to learn what you actually need right now. Your guidance will help us build the most relevant tools and topics over the next few weeks.

👉 Share Your Advice » (2 min)


Now, onto this week’s podcast…

 

If you keep second-guessing your type, it might not be you. It might just be the way the functions are described.

 

In this week's episode, we unpack how the MBTI system (and internet stereotypes) can quietly push people toward the “cool” functions and away from the ones they actually use, especially when you’re trying to self-type in community spaces.

 

👉 Listen now and discover how perceiving functions streroe
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕

In this episode, we explore:

  • Why Sensation (Se) is really about aliveness and direct experience (not just “adrenaline”).

  • How Perspectives (Ni) gets framed as “woo,” causing practical NJs to dismiss their own intuition.

  • Why Memory (Si) is unfairly painted as rigid, and how reviewing experience can sometimes look like Perspectives (Ni).

  • How Exploration (Ne) is oversold as chaotic genius, and what mature, grounded exploration actually looks like.

We’d love to hear from you:

 

👉 For you... which function do you think gets misrepresented the most, and why?

 

<— Hit reply and share your experience with us.

 

We released this podcast in both video and audio this week.
Watch or Listen To The Podcast ⮕
 


Much Love,

Joel Mark Witt & Antonia Dodge
Co-Founders | Personality Hacker
 

PS - Can You Share Your Advice...

We don’t want to guess what you need this Spring. Help us understand what’s most important to you right now.

Others in our community are already sharing what they’re facing right now. Join the conversation and help guide what we focus on this month.

You can also just hit reply and answer this question... "If you could make one thing easier in your life by the end of the month, how would you describe it?”

subject: Coaching, Contribution & the Legacy You Leave
body:
Many people step into coaching because they want to earn more.

There’s nothing wrong with that.

Growth matters.

Financial freedom matters.

Building something meaningful matters.

But the best coaches, the ones who truly build something extraordinary, get into coaching because they want to help people.

They want to see lives change.

They want to see confidence grow.

They want to see families lifted, futures expanded, and potential realised.

At the Champion Academy, that belief sits at the core of everything we do.

Yes, we teach people how to build sustainable wealth.

Yes, we believe you should create security and opportunity for yourself and your family.

But we also believe success means very little if it stops with you.

In 2025, through the support of our clients and the profits in our business, we’ve been able to give back in a way that reflects that belief.

We continue to support a school in Bali near where we run our retreat.

The children there have severe learning challenges, and your contributions are going towards the renovation of their physiotherapy room which is a space that will play a vital role in improving mobility, strength, and independence for these children.

Right now, the photos may not look like much.

But the impact this space will have will be astronomical.

Because when you improve a child’s physical capacity, you improve their confidence.

When you improve their confidence, you improve their future.

That’s legacy.

We believe in business for good.

We believe in giving back beyond yourself.

We believe in building wealth with purpose.

Around the world, wherever we run programs, we invest into charities and help build schools because coaching isn’t just about transactions.

It’s about transformation.

You only have one life.

One opportunity at this extraordinary thing called life.

And when you reach the end of it, you don’t want to look back and wish you’d played bigger or given more.

So I invite you to think about your legacy.

Not just how much you’ll earn.

Not just how far you’ll go.

But who will be better because you were here?

When you start thinking at that level, everything shifts.

You build stronger businesses.

You pursue excellence.

You invest in yourself.

You elevate your standards.

You create success that stands for something.

And from that place, coaching becomes more than a career.

It becomes contribution.

I’m excited to walk this journey with you and building not just income, but impact.

Your legacy is waiting.

No matter what happens

Never give up on your dreams

Ed

P.S. If you would like to learn more about the Mentari Jajar Foundation we support or you’d like to make even the smallest contribution you can do so here (https://d30-LD04.eu1.hubspotlinks.com/Ctc/GG+113/d30-LD04/VW6-j25C5x4NVTLllz3MxnG5W58c1_75KpDCfN6Q02s63lcq-W7lCdLW6lZ3nDW8YnNvC6-CplNW3wkvz74SX3FtN29qqdL1qClhW815sz62DZVDKW13_WhL1RVh6nW8jgxxx6_5bdVW5dj96b6FW8g8W3fC8dK3z559fW88Xw2835lw8CVDwWzT4Nwgc3V88XNt648TwCW4s6vry1RLk8QW2_BTTV6chgTXW3GBnww6Bpn-HW7FsgS-3kpNw7W28KDT37h0PRnW90HsfV2xJg0HW5BHBSH2cjQj_W1Xn9Qc9l3m2NW5LNKSR3gS3k6N4sXk6Bkyby5W6bmmJK8Q5gvCW8KkKmV1jGY1hW4SNvnY1Yf893f8NlvH004 ) .

subject: An Eyewitness Account of the Day a Leper Was Healed
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/an-eyewitness-account-of-the-day

Capernaum and the surrounding villages have grown accustomed to large crowds following the teacher from Nazareth. I had been traveling with the throng since early morning, documenting his movements, listening carefully to his words, and observing the response of the people. What occurred shortly after midday, however, demands more than casual mention. It demands record.
We were on a dusty stretch of road just outside a small settlement. The air was dry, the sun high. Farmers paused in their fields to watch as the teacher spoke about mercy, repentance, and the nearness of the kingdom of God. His voice carried steadily across the hillside. There was no spectacle in his manner. He spoke plainly, yet with an authority that caused even skeptics to fall silent.
Then the interruption came.
From the edge of the crowd a figure emerged, moving hesitantly at first, then with sudden determination. Several people recoiled. Others stepped back sharply, covering their faces. The man was visibly afflicted with leprosy. His skin bore the unmistakable signs of the disease. Patches were pale and cracked. Fingers appeared damaged. His clothing hung loosely and was torn in places, as required by custom. Under the law, he should not have approached at all. Lepers were to remain at a distance, declaring their uncleanness to warn others.
But this man did not cry out to clear the path. Instead he fell to his knees directly before the teacher.
The crowd gasped. Mothers pulled their children behind them. A few men shouted for him to keep his distance. One elder muttered that the teacher himself would now be defiled.
The leper bowed low, his voice trembling but clear. He said, Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.
There was no accusation in his words. No demand. Only conviction.
For a brief moment the scene held in tense silence. Any contact with such a man would render one ceremonially unclean. Even standing so near risked contamination. I positioned myself close enough to see the teacher’s expression.
He did not step back.
He did not call for others to remove the man.
Instead he extended his hand.
The motion was deliberate. Calm. Unhurried. He reached down and touched the leper.
Several in the crowd cried out in protest. One woman covered her mouth in shock. It was not only the healing that startled us. It was the touch. Compassion was evident on his face, not hesitation.
He said, I am willing. Be clean.
What happened next is difficult to describe without inviting disbelief. The change was immediate. The discolored patches began to fade. The rigid tension in the man’s posture gave way to astonishment. He looked at his own hands, turning them over as if seeing them for the first time. The deformities appeared restored. The skin looked whole. Healthy.
A murmur rippled through the gathering, rising quickly into open exclamation. Some fell to their knees. Others began to praise God aloud. A few stood frozen, unable to reconcile what they had just witnessed.
The healed man wept openly. He reached toward the teacher again, but the teacher gently instructed him to go at once to the priest and present the offering commanded by Moses as a testimony. It was a directive rooted in the law, a call to formal verification. This was no rejection of established authority, but an invitation for it to examine the evidence.
I followed the man at a short distance as he made his way toward town. People who moments earlier had avoided him now stared in confusion. Those who knew his condition could not deny the transformation.
In speaking with several witnesses afterward, I found no consensus explanation. Some claimed divine intervention. Others suggested unknown forces. A few refused to comment at all. Yet none could dispute the sequence of events. A man long identified as a leper approached in visible affliction. He was touched. He was restored.
As an observer, I record not rumor but what I saw. There was no elaborate ritual. No incantation. No extended ceremony. A request. A touch. A declaration.
And a cure.
Whether one interprets the moment as miracle, mystery, or something yet unnamed, the fact remains that on this road in Galilee, a man once separated from his community by disease walked away whole.
For those present that day, the greater astonishment may not have been the healing itself, but the willingness to cross the boundary first. The touch preceded the transformation.

  /*
      ------------------------------------
      EMAIL TABLE STYLES
      ------------------------------------
      - Cannot use position absolutes
      - Cannot use margin-top negative
  */

  /**UTILITY*/
  [data-ui-clearfix] {
      clear: both;
  }
  [data-ui-spacer] {
      height: 20px;
  }
  [data-ui-borders] {
    border: 1px solid #e6e6e6;
  }
  table[data-ui-wrap-parent],
  .tbl[data-ui-wrap-parent] {
    /*NOTE: This is necessary for word wraps and
     *      breaks to take effect on children
     *      elements. Use this for tables tags.
     *      Create new selectors for divs with
     *      receiving display:table, use .tbl
     *      consistently to avoid ever growing
     *      one off selectors*/
    table-layout: fixed;
  }
  div[data-ui-wrap-longword] {
      /*NOTE: Allow break on long words w/o spaces*/
      /*NOTE: Make sure to add this attributes on a div
       *      with a td parent*/
      /*NOTE: Finding that overflow-wrap: break-word;
       *      accomplishes the same thing as
       *      word-wrap: break-word; on Firefox and
       *      Chrome*/
      /*NOTE: Finding that word-break: break-word;
      /*      is not doing anything???*/
      /*NOTE: On some browsers this does not work
       *      by itself must be combined with
       *      word-break: break-word*/

      /*NOTE: Firefox, Chrome, Safari*/
      word-wrap: break-word;

      /*NOTE: IE11*/
      -ms-word-wrap: break-word;

  }

  /**OVERRIDE OUTLOOK*/
  .EmailClientBody {
    mso-line-height-rule:exactly;
  }

  /**EMAIL OUTER FILL*/
    .EmailOuterFill-inner {
      background: #F7F8F9;
      /* NOTE: 5% side paddings are intentional
       *       email will be difficult to read on
       *       mobile or narrow screens if we go
       *       with something like 40px*/
      padding: 20px 5% 0;
    }

  /**EMAIL OUTER*/
    .EmailSection-outer {
      background: #fff;
      margin-top: 20px;
    }
    .EmailOuterPage-outer {
      max-width: 720px;
      margin: 0 auto;
    }
    .EmailOuterPage-outer[data-ui-template="basic"] {
      max-width: 600px;
    }

  /**EMAIL HEADER*/
    .EmailTop {
      text-align: center;
      padding: 20px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
    }
    .EmailTop__text {
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
    }

  /**EMAIL HEADER BAR*/
    .Email-HeaderBar-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-HeaderBar-inner {
      border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0;
      border-color: #000000;
      border-bottom: none;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 30px;
      text-align: center;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }

  /**EMAIL BANNER*/
    .Email-Banner-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-Banner-inner {
      border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0;
      border-color: #000000;
      border-bottom: none;
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #ffffff;
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 20px;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }

  /**EMAIL SECTION HEADER*/
    .Email-SectionHeader {
      font-size: 24px;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding: 20px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text {
      line-height: 1.4;
      margin-top: 5px;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text-main {
      font-size: 18px;
    }
    .Email-SectionHeader__text-sub {
      color: #888F9F;
      font-size: 14px;
      font-weight: normal;
    }

  /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT*/
    .Email-SectionContent {
      color: #1F232F;
      font-size: 20px;
    }
    .Email-SectionContent-inner {
      padding: 20px 30px 30px
    }
    .Email-SectionContent__body .Email-SectionContent__body-text {
      margin-top: 0;
      margin-bottom: 10px;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT STRIPE*/
    .Email-SectionContentStripe {
      color: #1F232F;
    }
    .Email-SectionContentStripe-inner {
      padding: 20px;
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-SectionContentStripe__text {
      word-break: break-word;
      overflow-wrap: break-word;
      line-height: 1.4;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT - SUB BODY*/
    .Email-SectionContent__sub-body {
      font-size: 16px;
    }
    /**EMAIL SECTION FOOTNOTE*/
    .Email-SectionFootnote-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-inner {
      border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px;
      padding: 10px 20px;
      background-color: #e0e0e0;
      color: #8a8a8a;
      line-height: 1.4;
      border-top: 1px solid #dcdcdc;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote--footer .Email-SectionFootnote-inner {
      padding: 20px 30px;
      text-align: center;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-item {
      margin: 0 10px;
      display: inline-block;
    }
    .Email-SectionFootnote-item a {
      color: #8a8a8a;
      text-decoration: underline;
    }
  /**EMAIL ACTIONS*/
    .Email-Actions-inner {
      /*NOTE: bottom padding takes account for bottom
        margin applied to children buttons*/
      padding: 10px 20px 10px;
      border-top: none;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-Actions [data-ui-div-whitespace] {
      /*NOTE: This is whitespace adjustment that
       *      that will be ignored by Outlook on
       *      client/Windows*/
      /*NOTE: bottom padding takes account for bottom
        margin applied to children buttons*/
      padding-bottom: 10px;
    }
    .Email-Actions .Email-ActionButton__span {
      /*NOTE: This element and/or styles prevent
       *      buttons from being 100% width and
       *      allows buttons to wrap.
       *      These styles will be ignored by Outlook
       *      (client/Windows).
       *      In Outlook (client/Windows), this element
       *      will behave like inline block.*/
      margin-right: 10px;
      display: block;
      float: left;
    }
    .Email-Actions .Email-ActionButton__a {
      margin-top: 10px;
      display: block;
      color: #fff;
      text-decoration: none;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: .12em;
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 16px;
      border-radius: 3px;
      -webkit-border-radius: 3px;
      -moz-border-radius: 3px;
      text-align: center;
      background-color: #000000;
      border-top: 12px solid #000000;
      border-bottom: 12px solid #000000;
      border-right: 18px solid #000000;
      border-left: 18px solid #000000;
    }
  /**EMAIL SECTION CONTENT BUTTON*/
    .Email-SectionContentButtons .Email-SectionContentButton__span {
      /*NOTE: This element and/or styles prevent
       *      buttons from being 100% width and
       *      allows buttons to wrap.
       *      These styles will be ignored by Outlook
       *      (client/Windows).
       *      In Outlook (client/Windows), this element
       *      will behave like inline block.*/
      margin-right: 10px;
      display: block;
      float: left;
    }
    .Email-SectionContentButtons .Email-SectionContentButton__a {
      margin-top: 10px;
      display: block;
      color: #fff;
      text-decoration: none;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: .12em;
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 16px;
      border-radius: 3px;
      -webkit-border-radius: 3px;
      -moz-border-radius: 3px;
      text-align: center;
      background-color: #000000;
      border-top: 12px solid #000000;
      border-bottom: 12px solid #000000;
      border-right: 18px solid #000000;
      border-left: 18px solid #000000;
    }
    /**EMAIL FOOTNOTE*/
    .Email-Footnote-outer {
        border-collapse: separate;
        border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-Footnote-inner {
      border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px;
      padding: 20px;
      border-top: none;
    }
    .Email-Footnote {
      line-height: 1.4;
      color: #888F9F;
    }
    .Email-Footnote p {
      margin: 0;
    }
    .Email-Footnote p + p {
      margin-top: 10px;
    }
    .Email-Footnote a {
      color: #888F9F;
    }

  /**EMAIL BOTTOM*/
    .EmailBtm {
      /*NOTE: Left, right, and bottom podding is
      specific to whitespace symmetry necessary
      when children items wrap*/
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
      color: #676D7E;
      padding: 20px 10px 10px;
      text-align: center;
    }
    .EmailBtm ul {
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      list-style-type: none;
    }
    .EmailSection .EmailBtm li {
      margin-bottom: 10px;
      margin-left: 10px;
      margin-right: 10px;
      display: inline-block;
    }
    .EmailBtm a {
      color: #676D7E;
      text-decoration: underline;
    }
    /**EMAIL BOTTOM - DETACHED (THIS IS AN ALTERNATE STYLE)*/
    .EmailSection + .EmailSectionBtm {
      margin-top: 0;
    }

    .EmailSectionBtm-outer {
      color: #676D7E;
      text-align: center;
      background: transparent;
      border: none;
      max-width: 720px;
      margin: 0 auto;
    }

    .EmailSectionBtm .Email-Actions-inner {
      padding-top: 10px;
      padding-left: 0;
      padding-right: 0;
      border: none;
    }

    .EmailSectionBtm .Email-ActionButton {
      color: #fff;
      text-decoration: none;
    }
    .EmailSectionBtm .Email-Actions-outer + .Email-Footnote-outer {
      border-top: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .EmailSectionBtm .Email-Footnote-inner {
      padding-top: 15px;
      text-align: left;
      border-top: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
      border-left: none;
      border-right: none;
    }
    .EmailSectionBtm .Email-Footnote-outer + .Email-Bottom-outer {
      margin-top: 20px;
    }
    .Email-Bottom {
      color: #676D7E;
      text-align: center;
    }
    .Email-Bottom-inner {
      padding-top: 20px;
      padding-bottom: 20px;
    }
    .Email-BottomItem {
      margin-left: 10px;
      margin-right: 10px;
      display: inline-block; /*NOTE: Ignored by Outlook (client/Windows)*/
    }
    .Email-Bottom a {
      color: #676D7E;
      text-decoration: underline;
    }
    .EmailSection blockquote {
      border-style: solid;
      border-color: #C9CEDB;
      border-width: 0;
      padding-left: 12px;
      padding-right: 12px;
      border-left-width: 2px;
    }

    .EmailSection blockquote cite {
      font-style: normal;
      font-weight: 600;
      padding-bottom: 3px;
      display: block;
    }



  /**EMAIL REPLY CARD*/
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - COMMENT NUMBER*/
    .Email-ReplyCard__cmtnum {
      width: 60px;
      text-align: center;
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
      color: #888F9F;
      padding: 10px;
      border-bottom-left-radius: 2px;
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 16px;
      line-height: 1;
      border: 1px solid transparent;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - TIMESTAMP*/
    .Email-ReplyCard__timestamp {
      padding: 0 20px;
      color: #888F9F;
      border: 1px solid transparent;
    }
    .Email-ReplyCard__timestamp-text {
      margin-top: 10px;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - MAIN*/
    .Email-ReplyCardMain-inner {
      padding: 10px 20px 20px;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - TEXT*/
    .Email-ReplyCard__text {
      line-height: 1.6;
      /*NOTE: allow break on
      *       - long words w/o spaces
      *       - long urls*/
      word-break: break-word;
      overflow-wrap: break-word;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - MODERATOR*/
    .Email-ReplyCard[data-ui-moderator="true"] {
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
    }
    .Email-ReplyCard[data-ui-moderator="true"] .Email-ReplyCard__cmtnum {
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #fff;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY CARD - IMPORTANT*/
    .Email-ReplyCard[data-ui-important="true"] .Email-ReplyCard-inner {
      background-color: #FFFAE6;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #D8DCE5;
    }
    .Email-ReplyCard[data-ui-important="true"] .Email-ReplyCard__cmtnum {
      /*NOTE: These two selectors are attempting to check the same thing.
       *      prototype uses vue.js which omits "data-ui-moderator" from appearing at all
       *      including [data-ui-important="false"] just incase this is build differently
       *      for production code*/
      background-color: #FECB2F !important;
      color: #fff;
    }

  /**EMAIL REPLY FILE ATTACH*/
    .Email-ReplyFileAttach-inner {
      line-height: 1.4;
      padding: 20px;
      border-top: none;
      border-bottom: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .EmailSection .Email-ReplyFileAttach-inner > p {
      margin: 0;
    }

    .EmailSection .Email-ReplyFileAttach-inner > p + p {
      margin-top: 5px;
    }
    /**EMAIL REPLY FILE ATTACH - IMPORTANT*/
    .Email-ReplyFileAttach-outer[data-ui-important="true"],
    .Email-ReplyFileAttach-outer[data-ui-important="true"] .Email-ReplyFileAttach-inner {
      background-color: #FFFAE6;
      border-top: none;
    }

  /**EMAIL RECENT CARDS*/
    .Email-RecentCards-outer {
      /*NOTE: This outer wrapper should
      always be included for consistency.
      Purpose of this element will become
      more apparent for styles targeting
      specific set of reply cards.
      */
      /*NOTE: Fixed table layout will allow text wrap to occur*/
      table-layout: fixed;
      border-collapse: separate;
      border-spacing: 0;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard:last-child .Email-RecentCard-inner {
       border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard + .Email-RecentCard .Email-RecentCard-inner {
      border-top: 1px solid #e6e6e6;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard-inner {
      position: relative;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard-inner[data-ui-moderator="true"] {
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - RESPONDER*/
    .Email-RecentCardMeta-outer {
      table-layout: fixed;
    }
    .Email-RecentCardMeta-inner[data-ui-content="name"] {
        padding: 0 5px 0 20px;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard__responder {
        margin-top: 15px;
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - RESPONDER - NAME*/
    .Email-RecentCard__name {
        color: #4C5163;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 18px;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - TIMESTAMP*/
    .Email-RecentCard__timestamp {
      color: #888F9F;
      font-size: 14px;
      /*NOTE: create illusion of "perfect" 20px whitespace above response text...*/
      margin-bottom: 8px;
      display: inline-block; /*NOTE: Ignored by Outlook (client/Windows)*/
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - COMMENT NUMBER*/
    .Email-RecentCardMeta-inner[data-ui-content="cmtnum"] {
      background-color: #EEF0F3;
      color: #888F9F;
      padding: 10px;
      border-bottom-left-radius: 2px;
      width: 60px;
      text-align: center;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard__cmtnum {
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 16px;
      line-height: 1;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - MEDIA*/
    .Email-RecentCard__media {
      float: left;
      text-align: center;
      padding: 20px 0 20px 20px;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard__media-img {
      height: 28px;
      width: 28px;
      border-radius: 28px;
      display: block;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - META*/
    .Email-RecentCard-meta {
      /*NOTE: prevent strange whitespace
      *       when ellipsis occurs on
      *       surrounding elements*/
      display: inline-block;
      /*NOTE: avoid excessive whitespace
      *       caused when colliding into
      *       cmtnum div - cannot use
      *       position absolute reliabily
      *       in email*/
      max-width: 80%;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - TEXT*/
    .Email-RecentCard__text {
      line-height: 1.6;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - FILE ATTACH*/
    .Email-RecentCardFileAttach-inner {
      line-height: 1.4;
      padding: 20px;
      border-top: 1px solid #EEF0F3;
    }
    .EmailSection .Email-RecentCardFileAttach-inner > p {
      margin: 0;
    }
    .EmailSection .Email-RecentCardFileAttach-inner > p + p {
      margin-top: 5px;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - MODERATOR*/
    .Email-RecentCard[data-ui-moderator="true"] .Email-RecentCard__name {
      color: #000000;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard[data-ui-moderator="true"] .Email-RecentCardMeta-inner[data-ui-content="cmtnum"] {
      background-color: #000000;
      color: #fff;
    }
    /**EMAIL RECENT CARD - IMPORTANT*/
    .Email-RecentCard[data-ui-important="true"] {
      background-color: #FFFAE6;
    }
    .Email-RecentCard[data-ui-important="true"] .Email-RecentCard__timestamp {
      color: #b5b5b5;
    }

subject: [Care Ministry: Prayer Sheet] Prayer Sheet 2/10
body:
Prayer Sheet 2/10

A handful of months ago, I bought a bunch of Karen Kingsbury
books second hand and though they occasionally make me roll my
eyes because they can be a little cheesy, they are wholesome and
encouraging and I've been really enjoying them.

One of the themes and verses that comes up again and again is
Jeremiah 29:11 "For I know the plans I have for you," declares
the Lord, "plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to
give you a hope and a future."

And whether or not you're a Karen fan, that verse is always a
good reminder.

And an easy reminder to turn our gaze and hearts heavenward,
especially amidst all the chaos of every day life.

subject: 4th Grade News
body:
Hello Room 8 Families!

Sorry to bombard your inbox with school info but I have some exciting
auction news. If you have never joined in the fun at a Rio Del Mar Auction,
this is the year to attend. For the first time in the history of all
Auctions, our upcoming Masquerade Auction will have an OPEN BAR...ALL NIGHT
LONG!!!!! Yep...free drinks for all guests, all night! Come one, come all,
you don't want to miss this historical event! Get your tickets now (link
below) for early bird pricing. You won't regret it.

https://rdmpa.betterworld.org/events/rios-moonlight-masquerade

If you are in need of a fun option for child care, the Santa Cruz County
Parks & Rec has offered to host a Glow Night at Rio, run by our very own
after school ACE program. Nolan absolutely LOVES these Glow Nights. Link to
sign your child up below. Cost is $25 per child. There are only 26 spots
left.

https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/santacruzcountyparks/activity/search/detail/24301?onlineSiteId=0&from_original_cui=true

Last bit of auction news, we are still in need of donations to auction off.
Do you have a business or know someone who would like to make a tax
deductible donation?? Please let me know and I can provide you with the tax
form.

That's all for now. As always, please let me know if you have any questions!

Cheers,

Courtney
831.251.7707

subject: Planning Trips? We've Got Tips!
body:
Plan Now, Relax Along the Wayhttps://www.recreation.gov 

Whether it’s your first camping trip, a lakeside weekend with friends, or a family road trip, America’s public lands are the backdrop for memories that last a lifetime.

As we celebrate 250 years of adventure and wide-open spaces, there’s never been a better time to plan your next story. We’ve got the tips — you bring the journey.

**CHOOSE YOUR ADVENTURE:**

**⛺ 

**TENT CAMPING****

EXPLORE https://www.recreation.gov/search?inventory_type=camping&use_location=true&clear=true

**🚐 

**RV CAMPING****

EXPLORE https://www.recreation.gov/search?inventory_type=camping&campsite_type=rv%2F%20motorhome%2F%20trailer&sort=distance&use_location=true&clear=true

**GUIDE TIP**

Whether you're interested in tent or RV camping, use filters to narrow down sites based on site type, your vehicle length, and any other amenities that are important to you like fire pits, hookup preferences (electricity, water), waterfront spots and more!

**ENHANCE YOUR TRIP:**

**🎟️ 

**TICKETS AND TOURS****

EXPLORE https://www.recreation.gov/search?inventory_type=tickets+%26+tours&user_location=true&clear=true

**GUIDE TIP**

Once you've secured your campsite, check if there are any guided tours or ticketed experiences nearby to add to your trip and make it even more memorable!

**ARRIVE READY:**

**✅ 

**SITE PASSES****

EXPLORE https://www.recreation.gov/pass/#site-specific-digital-passes

**GUIDE TIP**

Consider purchasing a Site Pass to cover standard amenity (day-use) fees at the location you plan to visit in advance. This will save you valuable time for exploring when you arrive!

**MORE TIPS TO PLAN AHEAD AND PLAY MORE:**

The Face of the Architects
I have always maintained that history is not a line, but a circle. We are taught that the Neolithic Revolution was a slow awakening, but the latest intelligence coming out of the “Stone Hills” of Türkiye suggests something far more abrupt and far more technical.
In late 2025 and into these early weeks of 2026, archaeologists at Göbekli Tepe and Karahan Tepe have uncovered what I believe is the “User Interface” of the previous cycle. A human statue was found mounted horizontally on a wall at Göbekli Tepe, and for the first time in history, a T-shaped pillar at Karahan Tepe has been found with a clearly defined, carved human face, a sharp, angular jawline, and deep-set eyes that seem to be staring directly into our current timeline.
This is not “primitive” art. This is a monument to the Inherited Blueprint. These sites, dating back 12,000 years, were not built by hunter-gatherers who suddenly learned how to move 20-ton stones. They were built by the survivors of the previous reset, the “Watchers” or “Fallen Angels” of Secret History, and our theory. They were recording the face of the architects before they buried the site under thousands of tons of clean soil. They were archiving the “software” of their civilization because they knew the Frozen Cycle was beginning.
The Absolute Reset: The Tell Fara Break
To understand what is happening in Antarctica today, we must look at the recent findings from Tell Fara in Iraq (the ancient city of Shuruppak). Researchers have just identified a thick layer of yellow clay and sand, an “inundation layer” that points to a catastrophic flood nearly 20,000 years ago.
The lead archaeologists are calling it an “absolute culture break.” Below this layer, the craftsmanship is sophisticated, with proto-cuneiform and intricate polychrome jars. Above it, there is nothing for thousands of years. It is a total erasure. A hard reset of the human project. In Secret History and our theory, this is the moment the Intruders (The Hijack) took control, waiting for the ice to stabilize the new grid. But as we enter the 2026 window, that stabilization is failing.
The Signal from the Abyss
While the historians are looking at stones, the physicists are looking at the ice, and they are terrified. In late 2025, a startling report surfaced in Nature Communications regarding the ANITA (Antarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna). They detected mysterious radio pulses emanating from deep beneath the Antarctic ice.
These signals are not coming from space. They are rising from the bedrock at steep 30-degree angles, defying the known laws of physics. These are not neutrinos. These are high-energy pulses that suggest a Subsurface Source, an automated beacon from a hidden intelligence...

body:
Pacific Gas and Electric Company https://click.em.pge.com/? https://click.em.pge.com/? SB 1221 Informational Virtual Meeting https://click.em.pge.com/? VER EN ESPANOL 查看中文 Tingnan Tagalog Dear PG&E Customer: You are invited to participate in PG&E’s Virtual Information Session on Pilot Neighborhood Decarbonization Programs. The session will provide information on Senate Bill 1221 and the California Public Utilities Commission’s (CPUC) voluntary program to identify priority neighborhoods for potential projects that may transition some gas customers to cost‑effective, zero‑emission alternatives. February 26, 2026 at 4 p.m. (Pacific Time) Join Online Web link: https://click.em.pge.com/? Join via Teams Meeting ID: 249 722 867 341 31 Passcode: MQ7tx95J Join by Phone Dial: tel:1-415-906-0873 1-415-906-0873 Phone conference ID: 841 701 904# Note: If you need a language interpreter, please complete the following form at least five business days before the Information Session: https://click.em.pge.com/? https://click.em.pge.com/? Why Attend? Senate Bill 1221 allows up to 30 pilot projects across California to help transition some neighborhoods from natural gas to cleaner, zero-emission energy options. The CPUC is developing the rules for this program in Rulemaking 24-09-012. This virtual event gives you a chance to share your thoughts on which neighborhoods should be considered as priority decarbonization zones. These zones are areas where clean energy projects could be proposed in the future. We want to hear your input on local environmental hazards, access to heating and cooling, health considerations, community barriers to decarbonization, as well as your feedback on diversity and equity considerations outlined in Senate Bill 1221. How Would This Impact Customers? These efforts may influence future energy infrastructure and programs that support cleaner, safer energy options for communities, including disadvantaged and low-income neighborhoods. Alissa Macpherson and Bill McCart

NEW SMART PODCAST EPISODE: We don't leave any member behind
body:
New Talking SMART features discussion on SMOHIT, the SMOHIT Helpline and other resources for members

Even the strongest among us can fall: to exhaustion, to despair, to the weight of the fight. But in this union, we don’t leave any member behind.

In the third episode of Talking SMART season one, we’re joined by Sheet Metal Occupational Health Institute Trust (SMOHIT) Administrator Aldo Zambetti and Jeremy Holburn of the SMOHIT Helpline, a 24/7 helpline that SMART members and families can call whenever they need support (1-877-884-6227).

Brothers Zambetti and Holburn talk about the SMART Member Assistance Program (MAP), the resources available to members and local unions when it comes to mental health support, the importance of talking about your own experiences with mental health, and much more.

“We spent so much time dealing with on-the-job safety, workplace safety [in the past], and we sort of stayed away from work-life balance, we stayed away from things that make us not so safe. When we’re dealing with emotions, and depression, and anxiety, and any type of mental situation or emotional situation that we might be going through, and how it affects us on the jobsite.”

This season of Talking SMART focuses exclusively on mental health and the resources available to SMART members and their families. Make sure to subscribe on your preferred podcast program.
