subject: Fully Online Jungian and Archetypal Studies Program Apps Due
body:
Reflections on Dr. Lionel Corbett by Dr. Joseph Cambray and more

​
NEWS <https://www.pacifica.edu/pacifica-news/>       EVENTS <https://www.pacifica.edu/pacifica-events/>       HOME <https://www.pacifica.edu/>

          Are you fascinated by archetypes, symbols, and the unconscious forces that influence personal and collective experience? A path in Jungian and archetypal psychology might be for you.        

          Pacifica is currently accepting applications for the fully online Jungian and Archetypal Studies program <https://www.pacifica.edu/degree-program/jungian-archetypal-studies/> (DJO) for Spring 2026.         

Program Details:

	               The online track (DJO) has the same academic content as the hybrid low-residency track (DJA).            


	               Unlike the hybrid track, no on-campus residential attendance is required.            


	               The entire Jungian and Archetypal Studies program can be completed fully online.            


	               Each course is structured into 10 learning modules per quarter.            


	               Course materials include:            

	                   Recorded lectures                


	                   Assigned readings                


	                   Discussion boards for engagement with instructors and cohort                




	               Each course also requires four live online class sessions per quarter.            


	               Live sessions are designed for real-time instruction, discussion, and cohort interaction.            



          The program provides a unique opportunity to engage with, apply, and advance depth psychological theories and practices within the Jungian and archetypal traditions. Building on the work of C.G. Jung and James Hillman, students will consider approaches to the psyche that foster healing, transformation, self-expression, creativity, and the development of consciousness. Program co-chair Keiron Le Grice, PhD discusses more here <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-mHO2DJcwN8>.         

LEARN MORE <https://www.pacifica.edu/degree-program/jungian-archetypal-studies/>. 

Dr. Joseph Cambray Reflects on Dr. Lionel Corbett's Legacy

Dr. Joseph Cambray is a Past President and CEO of Pacifica, Jungian analyst, author, and past President of the International Association for Analytical Psychology. 

As a featured presenter at the 24th annual Jung in Ireland seminar <https://nyjungcenter.org/trip/jung-in-ireland-2026-study-tour/>—Facing Mortality and the Unknown—Dr. Cambray will explore themes central to the human psyche, uncertainty, the archetypal experience of mortality, and the life's journey toward meaning. This year's seminar is dedicated to the memory of beloved Jungian scholar and Pacifica Professor Emeritus, Lionel Corbett, whose work on the religious function of the psyche and the spiritual dimensions of depth psychology continues to inspire practitioners and scholars worldwide.

"Lionel also explored the ageing process, including later life psychological development and gerontological care. His pioneering work in this area has helped shape a more conscious, reflective approach to issues of mortality. His writings created a scholarly path towards deepening our appreciation of soul, mortality, and the afterlife, In this he also developed groundbreaking applications which directly expanded the therapeutic process around issues of later life. His legacy will indeed be informing this year's seminar."

READ FULL POST <https://www.pacifica.edu/pacifica-news/dr-joseph-cambray-reflections-on-lionel-corbetts-legacy/>

Sunday, March 15

Ask an Advisor Webinars

Questions about Pacifica? Join us for an Ask An Advisor webinar-- an opportunity for a live Q&A with our  Admissions Advisors.
Feb 18, & March 18
          FREE

REGISTER <https://www.pacifica.edu/pacifica-events/#1750715385615-59dafc27-9bce>

  Pacifica Extension Graduate Certificate:
Writing Down the Soul
          March 21, 2026 - December 13, 2026 
Featuring Maureen Murdock, Ph.D. and Jennifer Leigh Selig, Ph.D.

          Memoirs address the domains of myth: Who am I? Who are my people? What is my journey? What is my purpose? Where is home? The essence of a great memoir is the voice of the writer and how she brings the reader into a scene with sensory details.         

This Extension Certificate welcomes participants who:

	               Have always wanted to write a full-length memoir or try their hand at shorter personal reflections            


	               Have already written memoir pieces and want to bring a depth perspective to their writing            


	               Have a desire to cultivate a sense of archetypal and mythic consciousness in their writing            


	               Wish to honor a soul-filled perspective towards creative imagination            


	               Desire the structure and support a thoughtful writing community can offer            



REGISTER <https://extension.pacifica.edu/writing-down-the-soul-3/>

subject: The Human Spine Is an Antenna
body:
View this post on the web at https://anonymous8675309.substack.com/p/the-human-spine-is-an-antenna

Scripture teaches that the human body is not accidental. It is formed with purpose order and intention. We are told plainly that we are fearfully and wonderfully made and that the Creator knit us together with design and awareness.
The spine is not merely bone and nerve. It is the central pillar of the body and a living symbol of alignment between heaven and earth.
The Bible consistently reveals that posture alignment and uprightness are tied to authority obedience and spiritual clarity.
The Pillar Within the Body
The spine is the central column of the human form. Every nerve passes through it. Every signal from brain to body flows through it. When it is broken the body cannot function. When it is upright the body is capable of strength movement and endurance.
Scripture often describes righteous people as upright.
The Lord upholds all who fall and raises up all who are bowed down. Psalm 145
God does not merely comfort the bowed. He raises them upright.
The physical posture mirrors the spiritual condition.
Uprightness and Authority
Throughout the Bible standing upright is associated with readiness authority and divine commissioning.
When Ezekiel encountered the presence of God the Spirit entered him and set him upon his feet so that he could hear the voice speaking to him.
When Jesus healed the woman bent over for eighteen years the scripture says she was made straight and immediately glorified God.
Her bondage was visible in her posture. Her freedom was revealed in her alignment.
Christ did not only heal her body. He restored her ability to stand upright before God.
The Spine and Breath of Life
God formed man from the dust and breathed into him the breath of life and man became a living soul.
Breath and spirit are inseparable in scripture. The Hebrew word ruach means breath wind and spirit.
Breathing deeply requires an open chest and an aligned spine. When the body collapses breathing shortens. When the spine straightens breath expands.
Stillness alignment and breath create receptivity.
Be still and know that I am God.
Stillness is not inactivity. It is alignment.
Jacob’s Ladder and the Inner Ascent
Jacob dreamed of a ladder set upon the earth with its top reaching to heaven and angels ascending and descending upon it.
This image has echoed through theology for thousands of years because it reflects a truth woven into creation.
There is a vertical order to how God communicates.
Scripture repeatedly emphasizes upward motion.
Lift up your heads
Look up for your redemption draws near
Set your mind on things above
The body itself mirrors this divine architecture. A straight spine a lifted head and eyes oriented upward place the body in agreement with the posture of prayer expectancy and obedience.
The Body as a Temple
Scripture declares that the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.
A temple has order. A temple has alignment. A temple has a central column.
When the spine is compressed the body reflects burden and submission to weight. When the spine is upright the body reflects readiness and authority.
Stand therefore having girded your loins with truth.
Truth is not passive. It requires standing.
The Enemy and the Bent Posture
Oppression in scripture is often described as being bowed down burdened or crushed.
The enemy seeks to keep people bent distracted fearful and looking downward.
Modern life reinforces this posture through constant stress endless stimulation and downward focus.
A bent body produces a bent perspective.
But scripture calls believers to stand firm stand fast and stand in the day of trial.
Alignment as Obedience
Standing upright is not pride. It is obedience.
The humble stand before God because they trust Him to uphold them.
The righteous fall seven times and rise again.
Rising is part of faith.
When the spine aligns the breath deepens. When the breath deepens calm follows. When calm follows the voice of God becomes easier to discern.
God does not shout over chaos. He speaks in stillness.
Final Reflection
The spine is not worshiped. It is designed.
It is the central line through which life breath and command flow.
Stand upright before the Lord.
Lift your head.
Breathe deeply.
Be still.
Your body was designed to receive instruction.
A straight line receives clearly.
And God is a God of order.
